title: 5G Multicast Broadcast Services (MBS)
method: code on main read against every statement of the MBS User Services specifications on the project page, then every case read again independently by a second reader; disagreements settled by a third reading, otherwise not shown

reasons: a specification or code outside the audit that could not be read
it could not be settled by reading the code
the readers disagreed, so the case is not shown
the sentence applies to MBMS, which MBS does not use (MBS announces with TS 26.517)
the sentence states no behaviour a component could meet

requirements.name: Dynamic model / Notification events

cases.case: Notifications may be sent by different NFs during the session lifecycle
cases.what: The MBSF sends its own status notifications to subscribed consumers and receives and processes StatusNotify notifications from the MBSTF.

cases.case: MBSF may modify event information when passing on notifications
cases.what: The MBSF re-expresses MBSTF event reports as its own Nmb10 events (for example SESSION_DEACTIVATED becomes DIST_SESS_TERMINATED) and attaches the distribution session id before notifying the consumer.

cases.case: Events originating in the MBSF are propagated directly to the AF/AS
cases.what: Events the MBSF generates itself (user data ingest session starting, started, terminated, and user service advertisement) are put straight into a MBSUserDataIngStatNotif and POSTed to the subscriber's notifUri.

cases.case: Advertisement event carries external service identifiers for unicast mode
cases.what: The User Service advertisement event never carries the external service identifiers; for a service with the VIA_MBS_5 mode no advertisement event is generated at all, and the only event content is a carousel object URL in statusAddInfo.

cases.case: Advertisement event carries a URL for external delivery
cases.what: No advertisement event with a retrieval URL is produced for the passed-back (external delivery) mode; the announcement is returned inline in the ingest session response, and the only URL-bearing event is the carousel object locator sent when the announcement channel mode is used.

requirements.name: Nmbsf_MBSUserDataIngestSession_StatusNotify service operation / MBS User Data Ingest Session Status Notification

cases.case: MBSF sends notification request to a subscribed consumer
cases.what: When subscribed events are updated the MBSF builds a notification and sends it to the notification URI of the status subscription.

cases.case: POST to notifUri with MBSUserDataIngStatNotif
cases.what: The MBSF sends an HTTP POST to the notifUri stored in the subscription, with a JSON MBSUserDataIngStatNotif body holding the ingest session id and the event notifications.

requirements.name: Notifications / General

cases.case: Operation lets the MBSF notify consumers of ingest session status changes
cases.what: Status changes of the ingest session and its distribution sessions are turned into notifications POSTed to the subscribed consumer.

cases.case: MBSF may rescind an announcement
cases.what: There is no operation to rescind an announcement for operational reasons; it leaves the carousel only when its ingest session is deleted.

requirements.name: Procedures for 5G Multicast–Broadcast User Services / Procedures for User Service Announcement Channel provisioning

cases.case: Announcement channel provisioned with OBJECT_CAROUSEL
cases.what: The channel's distribution session uses the object method with the CAROUSEL operating mode.

cases.case: MBSF creates the channel session in the MBSTF via Nmbstf Create
cases.what: The MBSF creates the channel's distribution session in the MBSTF with the object method, carousel mode and push acquisition.

requirements.name: User Service Description data model / General

cases.case: Distribution Session Descriptions referencing a Session Description packaged in the bundle
cases.what: Each distribution session gets a description whose sessionDescriptionLocator names an SDP file that is written into the same bundle, optionally with repair parameters.

cases.case: Alternative Application Service Description objects
cases.what: The MBSF emits Application Service Descriptions with entry point locators for streaming object sessions; the entry point documents themselves are not packaged into the bundle.

cases.case: Descriptions document contains one or more User Service Description objects
cases.what: The announcement document is a single bare UserServiceDescription object, not a UserServiceDescriptions document wrapping an array of them.

cases.case: Each description includes at least one Distribution Session Description
cases.what: The user service description carries a distribution session description for every distribution session of the ingest session.

cases.case: Distribution Session Description refers to one Session Description document
cases.what: Each description has one sessionDescriptionLocator naming the SDP written for that distribution session.

cases.case: Distribution Session Description may include Object Repair Parameters
cases.what: Post-session object repair parameters are attached to object sessions when repair is configured.

cases.case: Application Service Description objects with entry point reference
cases.what: Zero or more Application Service Descriptions are emitted, each naming an entry point locator and content type.

cases.case: Only one Application Service Entry Point per Distribution Session Description in this release
cases.what: One Application Service Description is emitted for every acquisition id of a streaming session, so a description can reference several entry points.

cases.case: Service Schedule Description objects
cases.what: The announcement carries service schedule descriptions built from the ingest session's active periods or repetition rule; none are emitted when the session is always active.

cases.case: Time synchronisation and in-session repair references (Release 19 text)
cases.what: The description never references time synchronisation parameters or in-session repair parameters; only post-session repair is supported.

cases.case: Object Repair Parameters for in-session and post-session repair
cases.what: Only post-session repair parameters are produced; the in-session property is not in the Release 18 model.

requirements.name: Syntax and associated semantics / User Service Bundle Descriptions document

cases.case: version of the descriptions document
cases.what: No version number is written; the document has no wrapper to carry one.

cases.case: userServiceDescriptions array
cases.what: There is no userServiceDescriptions array; the document written is the single user service description object itself.

requirements.name: Syntax and associated semantics / User Service Description data type

cases.case: serviceIds
cases.what: serviceIds carries the provisioned external service identifiers as URIs.

cases.case: class
cases.what: class carries the provisioned service class URI.

cases.case: names array
cases.what: names carries one name entry per provisioned service name, each with its language.

cases.case: name
cases.what: Each name entry has name set from servName.

cases.case: Language of a service name as ISO 639-2 alpha-3
cases.what: The language is copied from the provisioned servNameDescs unchanged and never checked or converted to an alpha-3 code.

cases.case: descriptions array
cases.what: Descriptions are built only from entries that have a servName and read servDescrip unchecked: an entry with a name but no description raises an uncaught optional access error, and description-only entries are dropped.

cases.case: description
cases.what: A description entry is produced only when the entry also has a servName, and an entry lacking servDescrip raises an uncaught error instead of being skipped.

cases.case: Language of a service description as ISO 639-2 alpha-3
cases.what: The description list takes each provisioned servNameDescs language string unchanged (no ISO 639-2 alpha-3 check or conversion), and it reads servDescrip with an unchecked value after only a servName guard, so a servName-only entry raises.

cases.case: serviceLanguage
cases.what: serviceLanguage is never set in the announcement although mainServLang is provisioned.

cases.case: serviceScheduleDescriptions
cases.what: The array is built from the active periods or repetition rule; it is omitted when the session is always active, as the sentence allows.

requirements.name: Syntax and associated semantics / Distribution Session Description data type

cases.case: distributionMethod
cases.what: distributionMethod is set from the distribution session's method.

cases.case: sessionDescriptionLocator
cases.what: The MBSF sets sessionDescriptionLocator to the relative reference '<distribution session key>.sdp'; it is not an absolute URL.
cases.conflict: TS 26.517 table 5.2.4-1 types sessionDescriptionLocator as AbsoluteUrl ('URL to a Session Description document'), but its OpenAPI annex types it as the common Uri ($ref TS29571_CommonData.yaml#/components/schemas/Uri), which allows a relative reference; clause 5.3.1A allows relative Content-Location paths in bundles. No precedence rule was found in TS 26.517.

cases.case: applicationServiceDescriptions
cases.what: The array is present for object sessions in streaming mode and left out otherwise.

cases.case: availabilityInfos
cases.what: availabilityInfos is added when the session has target service areas or a frequency selection area id.

cases.case: distributionMethod is OBJECT when an Application Service Description is present
cases.what: Application Service Descriptions are only generated from object distribution info, so the method is OBJECT whenever they appear.

cases.case: Application Service Descriptions reference entry points of object sessions
cases.what: Entry point locators are built from the object distribution (or ingest) base URL and the acquisition ids of an object session in streaming mode; the content of those documents is the provider's.

cases.case: sessionDescriptionLocator points to the Session Description of the session
cases.what: The locator names the SDP written for the same distribution session, which carries the FLUTE delivery parameters.

requirements.name: Syntax and associated semantics / Session Description document

cases.case: Session Description may be packaged in the same bundle
cases.what: The SDP files are written beside announcement.json and added to the bundle served for the ingest session.

requirements.name: Syntax and associated semantics / Application Service Description data type

cases.case: entryPointLocator
cases.what: entryPointLocator is set to the entry point URI built from the base URL and acquisition id.

cases.case: contentType is a MIME content type
cases.what: contentType is derived from the file extension via the system MIME type table, falling back to application/octet-stream.

requirements.name: Syntax and associated semantics / Service Schedule Description data type

cases.case: Schedule Description delivered before the session and updated with the document
cases.what: The announcement bundle, with its schedule descriptions, is built when the sessions are established, before they become active, and rebuilt when the ingest session is updated.

cases.case: Distribution session available during announced intervals
cases.what: The MBSF moves each distribution session to ESTABLISHED shortly before and ACTIVE during each announced interval, and INACTIVE after, driving the MBSTF accordingly.

cases.case: Schedule description id
cases.what: Every schedule description of an ingest session uses the ingest session id as its id, so separate active periods share one id and differ only in version, instead of each session instance having its own invariant id.

cases.case: Schedule description version
cases.what: Versions come from a counter starting at 1 that only increases, and an unchanged period keeps its version across updates.

cases.case: Service schedule start date-time
cases.what: For each configured active period the MBSF writes a service schedule description whose start is the window start, as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time, in the announced User Service Description.

cases.case: Service schedule stop date-time
cases.what: For each configured active period the MBSF writes a service schedule description whose stop is the window end, as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time, in the announced User Service Description.

cases.case: cancelled flag of a schedule description
cases.what: The MBSF never sets cancelled on a service schedule description; a cancelled period is dropped from the schedule instead.

cases.case: start of a schedule description
cases.what: Each schedule description built from an active period has start and stop both set, and none has a repetition rule.

cases.case: stop of a schedule description
cases.what: Each schedule description built from an active period has stop set together with start, and none has a repetition rule.

cases.case: repetitionRule of a schedule description
cases.what: A schedule built from a repetition rule carries only repetitionRule, with no start or stop.

cases.case: repetition rule startTime
cases.what: startTime is copied from the repetition rule provisioned on the ingest session and also used to drive session states.

cases.case: repetition rule duration
cases.what: duration is copied from the provisioned repetition rule and used to drive session states.

cases.case: repetition rule repetitionInterval
cases.what: repetitionInterval is copied from the provisioned repetition rule and used to drive session states.

requirements.name: Syntax and associated semantics / Availability Information data type

cases.case: mbsFSAId in availability information
cases.what: The availability information carries the session's mbsFSAId when one is provisioned.

cases.case: nrParameters of availability information
cases.what: The MBSF never fills the NR transmission parameters of the availability information; only service areas and the frequency selection area id are set.

cases.case: freqBandIndicator
cases.what: The MBSF never builds NR parameter sets, so freqBandIndicator is never announced.

cases.case: aRFCNValue
cases.what: The MBSF never builds NR parameter sets, so aRFCNValue is never announced.

cases.case: nrParameters
cases.what: The MBSF never sets nrParameters in the availability information.

cases.case: nrRedCapUEInfo in availability information
cases.what: nrRedCapUeInfo is only copied into the stored session info and never announced.

cases.case: ncgiList in a target service area (Release 19 form)
cases.what: The MBSF never emits TargetServiceArea objects; service areas go out in mbsServiceAreas.

cases.case: taiList in a target service area (Release 19 form)
cases.what: The MBSF never emits TargetServiceArea objects; service areas go out in mbsServiceAreas.

cases.case: geographicAreaList in a target service area (Release 19 form)
cases.what: The MBSF never emits TargetServiceArea objects, so no geographicAreaList is announced.

cases.case: Exactly one of ncgiList, taiList, geographicAreaList (Release 19 form)
cases.what: The MBSF never emits TargetServiceArea objects, so the one-of rule is not applied.

requirements.name: Delivery of User Service Descriptions / General

cases.case: Bundle delivered via an MBS Distribution Session (MBS-4-MC)
cases.what: The bundle is delivered through the announcement channel distribution session.

cases.case: Bundle delivered by unicast at MBS-5
cases.what: There is no MBS-5 retrieval API for the bundle.

cases.case: Bundle delivered by application-private means (MBS-8)
cases.what: In PASSED_BACK mode the MBSF returns only the UserServiceDescription object to the Application Provider (mbsUserServiceAnmt); it builds no bundle for that mode, so the SDP documents the description's sessionDescriptionLocator names are never written or returned.

requirements.name: Delivery of User Service Descriptions / Delivery of User Service Descriptions Bundle Entity in object carousel

cases.case: Channel operating mode OBJECT_CAROUSEL with an object manifest
cases.what: The channel session uses CAROUSEL operating mode and the MBSF pushes an object manifest giving the repetition and keep-updated intervals of each bundle object.

cases.case: Manifest objects are User Service Bundle Entities
cases.what: The carousel object locator points to the bundle the co-located MBS AF serves as multipart/related, but that entity does not meet clause 5.3.1A: its Content-Type has only a boundary parameter, with no type parameter.

requirements.name: Delivery of User Service Descriptions / User Service Descriptions Bundle

cases.case: Each bundle resource has a URL and a MIME content type
cases.what: Each part of the bundle carries a Content-Location and a Content-Type header, the latter from a metadata file written beside the resource.

cases.case: Resources aggregated into a single multipart entity
cases.what: The bundle URL returns one multipart/related entity holding all resources.

cases.case: Each resource is a distinct body part
cases.what: Each file is added as its own body part with its own headers.

cases.case: Entity headers and body conveyed by different protocols
cases.what: The entity is served as the headers and body of an HTTP response and then carried as a multicast transmission object by the MBSTF.

cases.case: Compression of body parts or entity
cases.what: No part or entity is compressed.

cases.case: Entity Content-Type is multipart/related
cases.what: The entity's Content-Type is multipart/related with a boundary parameter.

cases.case: Root body part is a User Service Descriptions document
cases.what: The root part is announcement.json, a single UserServiceDescription object rather than a UserServiceDescriptions document.

cases.case: type parameter of the root body part
cases.what: The MBSF builds the bundle entity's Content-Type as multipart/related; boundary="..." and never emits a type parameter.

cases.case: Descriptions document is the first body part
cases.what: announcement.json is added to the serving list first, so it is the first body part, and no start parameter is used.

cases.case: Content-Location on every other body part of the bundle
cases.what: Each body part of the multipart/related bundle, including the SDP files, carries a Content-Location header holding its relative file name.

cases.case: No external references to directly referenced resources
cases.what: The Session Description documents the announcement references are in the bundle and referenced by a relative locator.

cases.case: Other body parts have a Content-Location URI
cases.what: Every part, including the SDP parts, gets a Content-Location header holding its relative file name, written inside double quotes.

cases.case: A User Service Descriptions Bundle Entity (hereafter "entity") shall conform to the ...
cases.what: The bundle is multipart/related with announcement.json first, but its Content-Type has no type parameter, its root part is a single UserServiceDescription object rather than a UserServiceDescriptions document, and Content-Location values are written in double quotes.

requirements.name: Announcement of MBS User Services / Encoding

cases.case: Descriptions document is a JSON instance of the schema in A.2
cases.what: The document is valid JSON but its root is a UserServiceDescription object, while the schema's root is UserServiceDescriptions with a userServiceDescriptions array.

cases.case: MIME type of the descriptions document
cases.what: The document is served with media type application/3gpp-mbs-user-service-descriptions+json.

requirements.name: HTTP protocol version / MBS AF

cases.case: MBS-1 endpoint follows the general HTTP provisions of 8.2.1.1
cases.what: The co-located MBS AF exposes an HTTP/1.1 endpoint only; it has no TLS support, which clause 8.2.1.1 requires.

cases.case: MBS-5 endpoint follows the general HTTP provisions of 8.2.1.1
cases.what: There is no MBS-5 endpoint for the User Service Description retrieval API.

cases.case: MBS-11 endpoint follows the general HTTP provisions of 8.2.1.1
cases.what: The MBSTF pulls manifests and bundles from the co-located MBS AF over an HTTP/1.1-only endpoint with no TLS support; the object locators use the http scheme.

cases.case: MBS AF Server header

cases.case: Retrieval API used when the announcement is advertised at MBS-5
cases.what: The MBSF offers no User Service Description retrieval API for services advertised at MBS-5.

cases.case: API base path {apiRoot}/3gpp-mbs-user-service-discovery/{apiVersion}/

cases.case: Operations and HTTP methods of table 9.2.2-1

cases.case: Sub-resource path appended to the base path
cases.what: The API base path and its sub-resources do not exist.

cases.what: The API operations do not exist; the bundle URL that does exist sets no ETag, Last-Modified or Cache-Control header and ignores conditional headers.

cases.case: Discover User Service Descriptions
cases.what: The discover operation does not exist.

cases.case: Retrieve User Service Description by externalServiceId
cases.what: The retrieve operation does not exist; bundles are fetched by ingest session id on an implementation-specific path.

cases.case: Discover response is a bundle entity of matching descriptions
cases.what: The discover operation and its response do not exist.

cases.case: Discover response bundle includes dependent resources
cases.what: The discover operation does not exist.

cases.case: Discover response: bundle headers in HTTP response headers
cases.what: The discover operation of the retrieval API does not exist.

cases.what: The MBSF has no Discover User Service Descriptions operation (no 3gpp-mbs-user-service-discovery API); it only serves announcement bundles from a docroot at /x-5gmag-service-announcements/v1/user-data-ingest-session/, and the bundle index response carries only a Content-Type header.

cases.case: Discover response: bundle body in the HTTP body
cases.what: The discover operation does not exist.

cases.case: Discover response may be gzip encoded

cases.case: This response message shall conform to the following requirements:
cases.what: The MBSF has no MBS-5 User Service Descriptions discovery service; the HTTP bundle at /x-5gmag-service-announcements is a different endpoint.

cases.case: Retrieve response is a bundle entity with a single description
cases.what: The retrieve operation of the retrieval API does not exist.

cases.case: Retrieve response includes dependent resources
cases.what: The retrieve operation does not exist.

cases.case: Retrieve response: bundle headers in HTTP response headers
cases.what: The retrieve operation does not exist.

cases.case: Retrieve response carries a strong entity tag
cases.what: The MBSF has no Retrieve User Service Description operation (user-service-descriptions/{externalServiceId}); only the docroot bundle path exists, whose index response sets no ETag.

cases.case: Retrieve response: bundle body in the HTTP body
cases.what: The retrieve operation does not exist.

cases.case: Retrieve response may be gzip encoded
cases.what: The retrieve operation does not exist and nothing is gzip encoded.

requirements.name: MBS AF APIs (MBS-1)

cases.case: MBS-1 protocol is HTTP as in 8.2.1.1
cases.what: The co-located MBS AF serves bundles over HTTP/1.1 but with no TLS, which 8.2.1.1 requires to be supported.

cases.case: The URL through which each MBS User Service Announcement bundle is exposed at ...
cases.what: The MBSF never sets a URL attribute for the bundle; for PASSED_BACK it passes the description inline in mbsUserServiceAnmt.

requirements.name: JSON-based representation / MBS User Service Announcement schema

cases.case: Descriptions documents identified with the registered MIME type

cases.case: profiles parameter of the media type

cases.what: The announcement.json is served with Content-Type application/3gpp-mbs-user-service-descriptions+json;version="Rel17", written as file metadata that the document server replays as a response header.

cases.what: The version parameter is "Rel17", not "Rel18".

cases.case: profiles parameter of the announcement media type
cases.what: The MBSF never emits the optional profiles parameter on the User Service Descriptions media type; only the version parameter is present.

cases.case: profiles parameter value as RFC 6381 productions with a fully-qualified term
cases.what: No profiles parameter is emitted, so no profile term is ever written.

cases.what: The generated enumeration has exactly VIA_MBS_5, VIA_MBS_DISTRIBUTION_SESSION and PASSED_BACK, and the code uses it for these modes.

requirements.name: Procedures for 5G Multicast–Broadcast User Services / Procedures for User Service Announcement Channel provisioning

cases.what: For pull acquisition in the manifest-based modes the MBSTF fetches the manifest and then re-fetches it on the manifest updateInterval (or the MPD minimum update period for DASH) from a background worker.

cases.what: For push acquisition the MBSTF starts a push ingest server and accepts an object only when its URL path equals the provisioned objAcquisitionIdPush (default "manifest"); other paths are refused with 400.

cases.case: User-Agent on pull-based ingest requests
cases.what: Differs from the requirement; the details are in the members-only section.

cases.what: The client acquires User Service Descriptions from the MBSF (MBS-5) or from a bundle received on the distribution carousel, and exposes service class, names and other parameters to the application.

cases.case: Query the MBSF over MBS-5 for additional access information

cases.case: Distribution Session Description objects

requirements.name: Syntax and associated semantics / User Service Bundle Descriptions document

cases.case: A higher version number overwrites a lower one

cases.what: The client carries the language of each service description through to the application.

cases.case: Ingest session creation with subordinate distribution sessions
cases.what: A POST on the sessions collection creates an ingest session and, for each subordinate distribution session that carries an SSM address, creates the MB-SMF session and then the MBSTF distribution session.

cases.case: No mbsSessionId: TMGI allocation requested
cases.what: A distribution session without an mbsSessionId is not given an MB-SMF session and no TMGI allocation is requested; TMGI is requested only inside the SSM path.

cases.what: For a distribution session with an SSM address the MBSF requests a TMGI from the MB-SMF when it creates the MBS session, and passes the locationDependent flag on to the MB-SMF.

cases.what: Once the MB-SMF sessions and MBSTF distribution sessions are set up, the MBSF answers 201 Created with a Location header made of the request URI and the new session identifier, and the session representation in the body; the resource is registered at creation.

cases.case: Failure handling and error status
cases.what: Most creation failures get an error status with problem details (400 for a malformed body or conflicting settings, the MB-SMF cause, an error when the MBSTF cannot create the session), but a distribution session of method OBJECT without objDistrInfo (or PACKET without pckDistrInfo) throws std::runtime_error from DistributionSessionInfo::validate, which the create handler (catching only std::out_of_range) does not catch, so no error response is sent.

cases.case: POST with MBSUserDataIngSession including mbsUserServId, mbsDisSessInfos, suppFeat
cases.what: The MBSF accepts a POST on the sessions collection carrying the MBSUserDataIngSession body; mbsUserServId and mbsDisSessInfos are mandatory in the generated model and the parent MBS User Service must exist, otherwise the request is rejected with 400; suppFeat is carried in the model but no feature negotiation is done.

cases.case: Active periods via actPeriods or actPeriodsRepRule
cases.what: Both actPeriods and actPeriodsRepRule are accepted and drive the active periods of the session; supplying both is rejected with 400, and with neither the session is always active.

cases.case: Update or modification of an Individual MBS User Data Ingest Session
cases.what: PUT on an individual ingest session updates it and propagates the changes to the MB-SMF and MBSTF; PATCH, the other half of the update/modification operation, is answered 404 'Method not allowed' and not applied.

cases.case: mbsSessionId, mbsDistSessId and locationDependent never updated
cases.what: On an update the MBSF keeps the old mbsDistSessionId, never copies mbsSessionId or locationDependent from the request, and silently ignores any change to them.

cases.case: Other attributes updated only when INACTIVE
cases.what: The MBSF applies changes to bit rate, delay, method, FEC, object and packet info, marking, external areas, flags and associated id only if the distribution session is INACTIVE; mbsServInfo, mbsFSAId and tgtServAreas are applied in any state, as the clause allows.

cases.case: Add new MBS Distribution Session in an update
cases.what: A distribution session whose map key is new in a PUT is added, registered, and its MB-SMF and MBSTF sessions are created.

cases.case: Remove existing MBS Distribution Session in an update
cases.what: A distribution session whose key is omitted from a PUT map is marked for deletion and removed, but the specified form (the existing key present with the value NULL) is treated as an unchanged present entry and deletes nothing.

cases.case: New distribution session added as a new map entry with a new key
cases.what: A map entry whose key is not an existing one is treated as a new distribution session, added to the session and created at the MB-SMF and MBSTF; a duplicate MBS session identifier is refused with 403.

cases.case: Removal of a distribution session through a NULL map entry
cases.what: A NULL map entry in mbsDisSessInfos of a PUT is treated as 'no change': the existing session is kept and the key is only dropped from the new-entries list; removal happens only when the key is omitted, and PATCH (where NULL entries are the removal mechanism) is refused with 404.

cases.case: Immutable attributes and INACTIVE-only attributes
cases.what: mbsSessionId, mbsDistSessionId and locationDependent are never changed by an update (the old identifier is kept and the others are not copied), and the remaining attributes are replaced only when the distribution session is INACTIVE.

cases.what: A PUT replaces actPeriods and the per-session mbsServInfo, mbsFSAId and tgtServAreas regardless of state, while other attributes are only taken over when the session is INACTIVE.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: MBSUserService

cases.case: extServiceIds
cases.what: The external service identifiers are required by the generated model, stored, returned with the service, and used as the service identifiers of the service announcement.

cases.case: servType: requested MBS service type
cases.what: servType is parsed and returned but is never used; the MB-SMF session is always created as multicast and the multicast or broadcast form of announcement is chosen from the presence of an SSM address.

cases.case: servClass: OMA BCAST service class term identifier
cases.what: servClass is stored in the model on creation and update, returned in the resource, and copied unchanged as the class of the announcement's user service description.

cases.case: servAnnModes: service announcement modes
cases.what: VIA_MBS_DISTRIBUTION_SESSION (announcement channel, refused with 400 when not configured) and PASSED_BACK (announcement returned to the provider) are acted on, but VIA_MBS_5 is accepted and stored with no handling, so nothing advertises the announcement at MBS-5.

cases.case: servNameDescs: per language name and description sets
cases.what: servNameDescs are stored and returned, but building the announcement names and descriptions fails for entries the API allows: an entry with servName and no servDescrip makes getServDescrip.value throw, and an entry with only servDescrip is dropped from the descriptions.

cases.case: mainServLang
cases.what: The main service language is stored, returned and used as the language attribute of the announcement session description.

cases.case: suppFeat negotiation in POST/PUT request and response
cases.what: No optional feature is defined for this API so no negotiation takes place; suppFeat is stored and echoed back as received.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: ServiceNameDescription

cases.case: servName
cases.what: The service name for each language is stored, returned and used as the name in the announcement; entries without a name are skipped for names.

cases.case: servDescrip
cases.what: The description list skips entries that have no servName instead of entries that have no servDescrip, so an entry with only a description is dropped and an entry with only a name makes the optional be read without a value.

cases.case: language
cases.what: language is required by the generated model and is used as the language of each name and description in the announcement.

requirements.name: Resource Standard Methods / PATCH

cases.case: PATCH modifies an existing Individual status subscription
cases.what: PATCH with application/merge-patch+json replaces the subscription's event list and/or notification URI when present in the patch and answers with the updated subscription.

cases.case: PATCH request body: MBSUserDataIngStatSubscPatch
cases.what: The PATCH body is parsed as an MBSUserDataIngStatSubscPatch and its eventSubscs and notifUri members are applied to the subscription.

cases.case: PATCH 200 OK with the updated representation
cases.what: After a successful PATCH the code answers 200 with the stored subscription as an application/json body.

cases.case: PATCH 204 No Content
cases.what: A successful PATCH always returns 200 with a body; there is no path that answers 204 for a status subscription modification.

cases.case: PATCH: headers of the 307 response
cases.what: The PATCH handler never answers 307, so no Location or 3gpp-Sbi-Target-Nf-Id header is produced.

cases.case: PATCH: headers of the 308 response
cases.what: The PATCH handler never answers 308, so no Location or 3gpp-Sbi-Target-Nf-Id header is produced.

cases.case: This method shall support the request data structures specified in table 6.2.3.5.3.3-2 ...
cases.what: PATCH on a status subscription accepts MBSUserDataIngStatSubscPatch as application/merge-patch+json and answers 200 with the updated representation.

requirements.name: Resource Standard Methods / DELETE

cases.case: DELETE removes an existing Individual status subscription
cases.what: DELETE removes the subscription's per-distribution-session event registrations and erases the subscription from the context.

cases.case: DELETE 204 No Content
cases.what: A successful DELETE of the subscription is answered with 204 and no body.

cases.case: DELETE: headers of the 307 response
cases.what: The DELETE handler never answers 307, so no Location or 3gpp-Sbi-Target-Nf-Id header is produced.

cases.case: This method shall support the request data structures specified in table 6.2.3.5.3.4-2 ...
cases.what: DELETE on a status subscription has no body and answers 204.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: MBSUserDataIngSession

cases.case: mbsUserServId: parent MBS User Service identifier
cases.what: mbsUserServId is a required member of the ingest session and is used to look up the parent MBS User Service, rejecting the request when it does not exist.

cases.case: mbsDisSessInfos: map of MBS Distribution Session information
cases.what: Each entry of the mbsDisSessInfos map becomes one distribution session keyed by the client-supplied string, and the same key is used in later updates.

cases.case: actPeriods give the active periods
cases.what: The MBSF converts the supplied time windows into active periods and moves each distribution session to ESTABLISHED before a window, ACTIVE inside it and INACTIVE after it.

cases.case: actPeriods omitted keeps the session active
cases.what: When no active periods or repetition rule are supplied the MBSF uses an always-active schedule with no end, so the session stays active until it is deleted.

cases.case: mbsUserServAnmt (deprecated object)
cases.what: The deprecated MBSUserServAnmt object is never populated; the code returns the mbsUserServiceAnmt (UserServiceDescription) form instead.

cases.case: mbsUserServiceAnmt returned only in PUT/PATCH responses when all sessions are ESTABLISHED/ACTIVE and PASSED_BACK is provisioned
cases.what: The announcement is set only when PASSED_BACK is provisioned and every distribution session is ESTABLISHED or ACTIVE, but it is also returned in the POST response and, being stored in the session object, in GET responses.

cases.case: mbsUserServiceAnmtUrl for VIA_MBS_5
cases.what: The MBSF never sets mbsUserServiceAnmtUrl and has no MBS-5 announcement service for the VIA_MBS_5 mode.

cases.case: suppFeat: feature negotiation
cases.what: suppFeat is parsed into the model and echoed back unchanged; the MBSF never reads it or computes a negotiated feature set.

cases.case: actPeriods: set of active time windows
cases.what: A list of time windows is used to schedule the distribution sessions: INACTIVE before, ESTABLISHED shortly before the window, ACTIVE inside it.

cases.case: actPeriodsRepRule: repetition rule
cases.what: A repetition rule (start time, duration, interval) is used to compute the ACTIVE/ESTABLISHED/INACTIVE state and the next transition.

cases.case: failedDistSessions
cases.what: The MBSF never builds failedDistSessions; any MB-SMF or MBSTF failure fails the whole request with a single problem response.

cases.case: redMbsServAreaInfo (Rel-18 form)
cases.what: The MBSF never returns the reduced MBS Service Area retained by the MB-SMF.

cases.case: NOTE 1: actPeriods and actPeriodsRepRule are mutually exclusive (POST)
cases.what: On creation a request carrying both actPeriods and actPeriodsRepRule is rejected with 400 and invalid-param entries.

cases.case: NOTE 1: actPeriods and actPeriodsRepRule are mutually exclusive (PUT)
cases.what: On PUT with both attributes the code silently uses actPeriods and ignores actPeriodsRepRule instead of rejecting the request.

cases.case: NOTE 2: no schedule means the session stays active until terminated by the AF
cases.what: With neither attribute the session is treated as always active and its distribution sessions stay ACTIVE until the ingest session is deleted.

cases.case: redMbsServAreaInfo (Rel-19/20 form)
cases.what: The MBSF never returns the reduced MBS Service Area retained by the MB-SMF.

cases.case: mbsUserServAnmt (deprecated object, Rel-20 text)
cases.what: The deprecated MBSUserServAnmt object is never populated; the code returns the mbsUserServiceAnmt (UserServiceDescription) form instead.

cases.case: mbsUserServiceAnmt returned only in PUT/PATCH responses (Rel-20 text)
cases.what: The announcement is set only when PASSED_BACK is provisioned and every distribution session is ESTABLISHED or ACTIVE, but it is also returned in the POST response and in GET responses.

cases.case: mbsUserServiceAnmtUrlExt (Rel-20 attribute)
cases.what: The attribute does not exist in the Rel-18 API the build pins and is never produced.

cases.case: mbsUserServiceAnmtUrl for VIA_MBS_5 (Rel-20 text)
cases.what: The MBSF never sets mbsUserServiceAnmtUrl and has no MBS-5 announcement service for the VIA_MBS_5 mode.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: MBSDistributionSessionInfo

cases.case: mbsDistSessionId present in creation and update responses
cases.what: The id is a UUID set when the MBSTF create request is built and is in the 201 body, but GET of the ingest session returns it too, and a distribution session added by PUT has no id in the immediate 200 response.

cases.case: mbsDistSessState only in POST/PUT/PATCH responses
cases.what: The state is returned in POST and PUT responses but also in GET responses, and a client-supplied mbsDistSessState in a request is honoured as the desired state.

cases.case: mbsSessionId: SSM and/or TMGI of the MBS Session
cases.what: An SSM mbsSessionId is kept and the MB-SMF-allocated TMGI is added to it, but a distribution session whose mbsSessionId is TMGI-only (or absent) is never created, and a TMGI supplied by the AF is overwritten by the allocated one.

cases.case: mbsServInfo: MBS Service Information
cases.what: mbsServInfo is converted and passed to the MB-SMF in the MBS Session create/update.

cases.case: maxContBitRate: maximum bit rate of the distribution session
cases.what: maxContBitRate is passed to the MBSTF as the distribution session bit rate and used as the bandwidth in the generated SDP.

cases.case: maxContDelay: maximum end-to-end delay
cases.what: maxContDelay is passed to the MBSTF as the distribution session maximum delay.

cases.case: distrMethod: OBJECT or PACKET
cases.what: distrMethod selects the object or packet distribution data sent to the MBSTF and requires the matching objDistrInfo or pckDistrInfo.

cases.case: objDistrInfo present when distrMethod is OBJECT
cases.what: For OBJECT the code requires objDistrInfo, but by throwing std::runtime_error in the DistributionSessionInfo constructor, which the POST handler does not catch (it catches only std::out_of_range), so no error response is built; objDistrInfo on a non-OBJECT session is not rejected.

cases.case: pckDistrInfo present when distrMethod is PACKET
cases.what: For PACKET the code requires pckDistrInfo, but by throwing std::runtime_error from the DistributionSessionInfo constructor, uncaught by the POST handler, so no error response is built; pckDistrInfo on a non-PACKET session is not rejected.

cases.case: trafficMarkingInfo carried to the MBSTF
cases.what: trafficMarkingInfo is passed to the MBSTF as the distribution session DSCP marking.

cases.case: tgtServAreas
cases.what: The MBSF uses the target service areas as the service area of the MBS session it requests from the MB-SMF and announces them as availability information.

cases.case: extTgtServAreas
cases.what: The MBSF passes the external target service areas to the MB-SMF as the external service area of the MBS session.

cases.case: mbsFSAId
cases.what: The MBSF passes the frequency selection area id to the MB-SMF and announces it in the availability information.

cases.case: locationDependent flag
cases.what: locationDependent is passed to the MB-SMF in the MBS Session; when omitted it is not set, which leaves the MB-SMF default of false.

cases.case: restrictedFlag
cases.what: restrictedFlag true gives any_ue_ind false (restricted) and false gives any_ue_ind true, because setAnyUeInd stores the negated value (reading 1's claim of no inversion is wrong).

cases.case: NOTE 1: TMGI allocated by the MBSF when mbsSessionId is absent
cases.what: A distribution session without an mbsSessionId carrying an SSM address is never provisioned, so no TMGI is allocated for it.

cases.case: NOTE 2: SSM only with locationDependent true: TMGI allocated and returned
cases.what: For an SSM-only mbsSessionId the MBSF always requests a TMGI from the MB-SMF and returns it in the response mbsSessionId.

cases.case: NOTE 3: objDistrInfo and pckDistrInfo are mutually exclusive, one shall be present
cases.what: Only the member matching distrMethod is required; a request carrying both is accepted and a missing one is not answered with an error.

cases.case: NOTE 4: tgtServAreas and extTgtServAreas are mutually exclusive
cases.what: Nothing checks that tgtServAreas and extTgtServAreas are not both present; both are accepted and both passed to the MB-SMF.

cases.case: associatedSessionId passed to the core network
cases.what: associatedSessionId from the distribution session information is converted and set on the MBS Session sent to the MB-SMF.

cases.case: nrRedCapUeInfo: NR RedCap UE information
cases.what: nrRedCapUeInfo is parsed and echoed in responses but never passed to the MB-SMF or used in the announcement.

cases.case: tgtServAreas: MBS Service Area of the distribution session
cases.what: tgtServAreas is converted to an MB-SMF MBS service area, used for the uniqueness check of the MBS Session and placed in the announcement availability information.

cases.case: extTgtServAreas: external MBS Service Area
cases.what: extTgtServAreas is converted to an MB-SMF external service area and used in the MBS Session uniqueness check.

cases.case: mbsFSAId: frequency selection assistance information
cases.what: mbsFSAId is parsed as a hexadecimal identifier and set on the MB-SMF MBS Session, and is also put in the announcement availability information.

cases.case: mbsDistSessState with 5MBS3 (GET response)
cases.what: The 5MBS3 feature (Rel-20) is not part of the Rel-18 API the build pins and is not negotiated; the state is returned in POST, PUT and GET responses without feature negotiation.

cases.case: transSecFlag: transport security required indication
cases.what: transSecFlag is not part of the Rel-18 model and is never read or produced.

cases.case: conformProfiles: content conformance profiles
cases.what: The ingest-session attribute conformProfiles is not part of the Rel-18 model and is never read; announcements carry a fixed baseline profile instead.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch

cases.case: actPeriods in the patch body
cases.what: The MBSF has no PATCH handling for the ingest session, so the patch form of actPeriods is never read.

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch.mbsDisSessInfos
cases.what: PATCH on an Individual MBS User Data Ingest Session is not implemented: it is answered 404 with a method-not-allowed message.

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch deprecated when MBSPatchEnh is supported
cases.what: Neither MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch nor MBSUserDataIngSessionPatchEnh is handled because PATCH on the ingest session is not implemented.

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch.actPeriods
cases.what: Updated active periods can only be sent by PUT; PATCH on the ingest session is rejected.

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch.actPeriodsRepRule
cases.what: An updated repetition rule can only be sent by PUT; PATCH on the ingest session is rejected.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: ObjectDistrMethInfo

cases.case: ObjectDistrMethInfo.operatingMode
cases.what: The operating mode is passed to the MBSTF and used to decide whether announcement entry points are built (STREAMING).

cases.case: ObjectDistrMethInfo.objAcqMethod
cases.what: The acquisition method (PULL or PUSH) is passed to the MBSTF and decides how the acquisition identifiers are sent.

cases.case: objAcqIds
cases.what: The MBSF forwards the acquisition ids to the MBSTF as the pull ids, or as the push id for PUSH, relative to the ingest base URL.

cases.case: objIngUri carried to the MBSTF
cases.what: objIngUri is passed to the MBSTF as the object ingest base URL, and the MBSTF performs the prefix replacement.

cases.case: objIngUri required when objDistrUri is present
cases.what: The code does not check that objIngUri is present when objDistrUri is given.

cases.case: objDistrUri carried to the MBSTF
cases.what: objDistrUri is passed to the MBSTF as the object distribution base URL and is also used as the entry-point prefix in announcements.

cases.case: NOTE 2: objIngUri provided by the AF for PULL
cases.what: For PULL the MBSF takes objIngUri from the AF's request and passes it to the MBSTF as the object ingest base URL.

cases.case: NOTE 2: objIngUri provided by the MBSF for PUSH
cases.what: The step that copies the MBSTF's ingest base URL into objIngUri for PUSH tests the operating mode against the string "PUSH" instead of the acquisition method, so it never runs and objIngUri is not returned for PUSH.

cases.case: NOTE 3: objDistrUri omitted
cases.what: When the AF omits objDistrUri the MBSF sets no distribution base URL, and the announced entry points use the ingest base URL unchanged.

cases.case: objAcqIds: root object identifiers
cases.what: For PULL the acquisition identifiers are sent to the MBSTF as a list; for PUSH the first identifier is sent as the push identifier.

cases.case: contentTypes: expected MIME content types of root objects
cases.what: contentTypes is a Rel-20 attribute that is not in the Rel-18 model and is never read.

cases.case: NOTE 1: Void. NOTE 2: When the "objAcqMethod" attribute is set to "PULL", this attribute m
cases.what: For PULL the AF value of objIngUri is carried, but for the push case the MBSF should return the MBSTF-chosen ingest base URL and the code tests the operating mode for the string "PUSH" (never true; modes are SINGLE, COLLECTION, CAROUSEL, STREAMING), so objIngUri is never filled from the MBSTF response.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: PacketDistrMethInfo

cases.case: PacketDistrMethInfo.operatingMode
cases.what: The packet distribution operating mode is passed to the MBSTF and PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY suppresses the traffic flow information.

cases.case: pckIngMethod: packet ingest method
cases.what: The packet ingest method (UNICAST or MULTICAST) is passed to the MBSTF.

cases.case: pckIngMethod: only UNICAST applies with PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY
cases.what: The combination of PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY with MULTICAST ingest is not checked or rejected.

cases.case: ingEndpointAddrs: ingest endpoint addresses at Nmb8
cases.what: The AF-supplied ingest address structure is passed to the MBSTF and the MBSTF listen and tunnel addresses it returns are merged into the response.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type MBSUserDataIngStatSubsc

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngStatSubsc.mbsIngSessionId
cases.what: mbsIngSessionId is required, must name an existing ingest session (else 400) and links the subscription to that session.

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngStatSubsc.eventSubscs
cases.what: The subscribed events are registered on the ingest session or on the named distribution sessions and drive which notifications are sent.

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngStatSubsc.notifUri
cases.what: Notifications are posted to the notifUri of the subscription.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type SubscribedEvent

cases.case: SubscribedEvent.statusEvent
cases.what: The subscribed status event selects which timestamp the subscription watches; only some event values are ever generated by the MBSF.

cases.case: SubscribedEvent.mbsDistSessionId
cases.what: When mbsDistSessionId is given the event is attached to that distribution session, and a creation request naming an unknown distribution session is rejected with 400.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type MBSUserDataIngStatNotif

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngStatNotif.mbsIngSessionId
cases.what: Each notification carries the identifier of the ingest session the subscription belongs to.

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngStatNotif.eventNotifs
cases.what: Each notification carries the list of reported events built since the last notification.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type EventNotification

cases.case: EventNotification.statusEvent
cases.what: Each reported event carries the status event value that was subscribed to.

cases.case: EventNotification.mbsDisSessionId
cases.what: Events reported for a distribution session carry its identifier, while session-level events omit it.

cases.case: EventNotification.mbsSessionId
cases.what: The MBS Session identifier is never put in a reported event.

cases.case: EventNotification.statusAddInfo
cases.what: statusAddInfo is filled for the USER_SER_AD event with the locator of the announcement bundle and is otherwise omitted.

cases.case: EventNotification.timeStamp
cases.what: Each reported event carries the time the event was observed, in ISO 8601 UTC form.

cases.case: mbsUserServiceAnmtUrlExt in an event notification (Rel-20)
cases.what: The attribute does not exist in the Rel-18 EventNotification and is not produced; the bundle locator travels in statusAddInfo of USER_SER_AD instead.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type MBSUserServAnmt

cases.case: MBSUserServAnmt.extServiceId
cases.what: The deprecated MBSUserServAnmt object is never built; the announcement is delivered as UserServiceDescription (serviceIds) instead.

cases.case: MBSUserServAnmt.servClass
cases.what: The deprecated MBSUserServAnmt object is never built; the service class is delivered in UserServiceDescription instead.

cases.case: MBSUserServAnmt.startTime
cases.what: The deprecated MBSUserServAnmt object is never built, so no announcement start time is produced.

cases.case: MBSUserServAnmt.endTime
cases.what: The deprecated MBSUserServAnmt object is never built, so no announcement end time is produced.

cases.case: MBSUserServAnmt.mbsDistSessAnmt
cases.what: The map of MBSDistSessionAnmt is never built; distribution session descriptions are produced in UserServiceDescription instead.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type MBSDistSessionAnmt

cases.case: MBSDistSessionAnmt.mbsSessionId
cases.what: MBSDistSessionAnmt is never built; the TMGI and SSM of a session appear only in the generated SDP file.

cases.case: MBSDistSessionAnmt.mbsFSAId
cases.what: MBSDistSessionAnmt is never built; mbsFSAId is placed in the availability information of the UserServiceDescription instead.

cases.case: MBSDistSessionAnmt.distrMethod
cases.what: MBSDistSessionAnmt is never built; the distribution method is placed in the DistributionSessionDescription instead.

cases.case: MBSDistSessionAnmt.objDistrAnnInfo
cases.what: ObjectDistMethAnmtInfo is never built.

cases.case: MBSDistSessionAnmt.sesDesInfo
cases.what: MBSDistSessionAnmt is never built; the session description is delivered as an SDP file referenced by sessionDescriptionLocator in the UserServiceDescription.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type ObjectDistMethAnmtInfo

cases.case: ObjectDistMethAnmtInfo.objDistrSched
cases.what: No object delivery schedule is produced for announcements.

cases.case: ObjectDistMethAnmtInfo.objDistrBaseUri
cases.what: ObjectDistMethAnmtInfo is never built; the distribution base locator for repair is produced in ObjectRepairParameters instead.

cases.case: ObjectDistMethAnmtInfo.objRepBaseUri
cases.what: ObjectDistMethAnmtInfo is never built; the repair base locator is produced in ObjectRepairParameters instead.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: FECConfig

cases.case: AddFecParams: additional AL-FEC parameters
cases.what: The AL-FEC configuration, including additional name/value parameters, is passed to the MBSTF unchanged.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type MBSUserDataIngStatSubscPatch

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngStatSubscPatch.eventSubscs
cases.what: An eventSubscs list in the patch replaces the subscribed events and the per-session registrations are rebuilt.

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngStatSubscPatch.notifUri
cases.what: A notifUri in the patch replaces the notification URI and the notification client is reset.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type MbsDistSessFailure

cases.case: MbsDistSessFailure.cause
cases.what: Per-distribution-session failure causes are never produced.

cases.case: MbsDistSessFailure.redMbsServArea
cases.what: The reduced MBS Service Area is never returned.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type MbsDistSessFailureSets

cases.case: MbsDistSessFailureSets.causes
cases.what: The per-distribution-session failure map is never produced.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: MBSUserDataIngSessionPatchEnh

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngSessionPatchEnh.actPeriodsRepRule
cases.what: PATCH on the ingest session is not implemented, so the enhanced patch type is not handled.

cases.case: MBSUserDataIngSessionPatchEnh.mbsDisSessInfos
cases.what: PATCH on the ingest session is not implemented, so individual distribution session modification and removal by patch is not handled.

requirements.name: Simple data types and enumerations / Enumeration: DistributionMethod

cases.case: DistributionMethod enumeration
cases.what: The OBJECT and PACKET values are in the generated enumeration and drive the object and packet handling.

requirements.name: Simple data types and enumerations / Enumeration: Event

cases.case: Event enumeration
cases.what: All sixteen Event values of the Rel-18 enumeration are accepted and tracked per subscription, although some are never generated.

requirements.name: Simple data types and enumerations / Enumeration: DistSessionFailure

cases.case: DistSessionFailure enumeration
cases.what: The enumeration is part of the generated Rel-18 model with all its values, although no code path ever produces a failure cause of this type.

requirements.name: Data types describing alternative data types or combinations of data types / Type: ProblemDetailsMBS

cases.case: ProblemDetailsMBS: ProblemDetails content
cases.what: Error responses are sent as application/problem+json carrying status, title, detail, instance, cause and invalid parameters in the TS 29.571 ProblemDetails form.

cases.case: ProblemDetailsMBS.mbsErrorInfo
cases.what: The MBS related additional error information for partial distribution session failures is never added to error responses.

requirements.name: Error Handling / General

cases.case: HTTP error responses as in TS 29.501 clause 4.8
cases.what: Failures are answered with ProblemDetails bodies and the status code mapped from a registered cause, e.g. 400, 404, 415 and 500.

requirements.name: Nmbsf_MBSUserDataIngestSession Service API / Feature negotiation

cases.case: 5MBS2: provisioning of the Associated Session Identifier
cases.what: associatedSessionId is accepted and passed to the MB-SMF in the MBS Session.

cases.case: 5MBS2: provisioning of NR RedCap UE Information
cases.what: nrRedCapUeInfo is accepted in the model but never passed to the MB-SMF or announced.

cases.case: 5MBS2: active periods as a repetition rule
cases.what: actPeriodsRepRule drives the ESTABLISHED, ACTIVE and INACTIVE states of the distribution sessions.

cases.case: MBSEventsExt: additional status events
cases.what: Some of the extended events (DIST_SESS_ACTIVATED, USER_SER_AD, SESSION_TERMINATED) are reported but DELIVERY_STARTED, SESSION_STARTED, SESSION_RELEASED, DIST_SESS_EST_FAILURE, DIST_SESS_STARTED and DIST_SESS_POL_CRTL_FAILURE are accepted in subscriptions and never reported, and the feature is not advertised.

cases.case: MBSErrorHandling: relaying MBS Session errors end to end
cases.what: MB-SMF failure causes that are in a small propagation table are relayed as status and cause, but the detail text is always the 'already exists in the MBS System' message, the MB-SMF ProblemDetails are not forwarded, MBS_SERVICE_AREA_NOT_SUPPORTED is never produced, and other causes become 502.

cases.case: MBSErrorHandling: partial creation/update failure management
cases.what: A failure of one distribution session fails the whole request; failedDistSessions and redMbsServAreaInfo are never produced.

cases.case: 5MBS3: retrieval and reporting of the announcement bundle
cases.what: The Rel-20 attributes for retrieving the bundle (mbsUserServiceAnmtUrlExt in GET and notifications) are not in the Rel-18 API and are not produced.

cases.case: 5MBS3: transport security protection indication
cases.what: transSecFlag is not in the Rel-18 model and is never read.

cases.case: 5MBS3: conformance profiles of the distributed content
cases.what: The ingest-session conformProfiles attribute is not in the Rel-18 model and is never read.

cases.case: 5MBS3: expected MIME content types in object distribution information
cases.what: contentTypes is not in the Rel-18 model and is never read.

requirements.name: (normative): OpenAPI specification / Nmbsf_MBSUserService API

cases.case: Retrieve all MBS User Services (collection GET)
cases.what: GET on the mbs-user-services collection is answered 400 invalid resource; no list is returned.

cases.case: 200 with all active MBS User Services
cases.what: No code path returns the array of active MBS User Services.

cases.case: POST request body: new MBS User Service
cases.what: POST on mbs-user-services requires application/json, parses the body as an MBSUserService and creates the service.

cases.case: 201 body: created Individual MBS User Service
cases.what: The 201 response carries the created MBS User Service representation as application/json.

cases.case: Location header of the created MBS User Service
cases.what: The 201 response sets Location to the request URI followed by the new service identifier.

cases.case: Path parameter: Individual MBS User Service identifier
cases.what: The second path component is used as the identifier of the Individual MBS User Service resource.

cases.case: Retrieve an existing Individual MBS User Service
cases.what: GET with an identifier returns the stored MBS User Service, or 404 when it does not exist.

cases.case: 200 with the requested MBS User Service
cases.what: The 200 response carries the MBS User Service as application/json with caching headers.

cases.case: Update an existing Individual MBS User Service (PUT)
cases.what: PUT replaces the stored MBS User Service with the body, or answers 404 when the service does not exist.

cases.case: PUT body: updated MBS User Service
cases.what: The PUT body is parsed as an MBSUserService and replaces the stored one.

cases.case: PUT 200: successfully updated, representation returned (first part)
cases.what: A successful PUT is answered with 200 and the updated representation.

cases.case: PUT 200: representation returned in the response body (second part)
cases.what: The 200 response body holds the updated MBS User Service.

cases.case: PUT 204 No Content
cases.what: PUT on an MBS User Service never answers 204.

cases.case: Modify an existing Individual MBS User Service (PATCH)
cases.what: PATCH on an MBS User Service is not handled; any method other than POST, GET, PUT and DELETE gets 400.

cases.case: PATCH 200: successfully modified, representation returned
cases.what: There is no PATCH handling for MBS User Services.

cases.case: PATCH 204: successfully modified
cases.what: There is no PATCH handling for MBS User Services.

cases.case: Delete an existing Individual MBS User Service
cases.what: DELETE first removes every ingest session of the service and then deletes the service, or answers 404 when it does not exist.

cases.case: DELETE 204: successfully deleted
cases.what: Once the service and its ingest sessions are gone the DELETE is answered 204.

cases.case: VIA_MBS_5 announcement mode
cases.what: The MBSF accepts VIA_MBS_5 in a provisioned service but does nothing for it: no announcement bundle is built and no MBS-5 announcement API exists.

cases.case: VIA_MBS_DISTRIBUTION_SESSION announcement mode
cases.what: For this mode the MBSF builds the announcement bundle, serves it from its co-located MBS AF and carries it over a dedicated announcement distribution session via the MBSTF.

cases.case: PASSED_BACK announcement mode

cases.case: Update the set of active periods at any time
cases.what: The provider never sets or updates active periods; its ingest session update sends only the user service id, one distribution session and a feature string.

cases.case: Active periods of the ingest session
cases.what: The provider never sends active periods, so its ingest sessions are always active until further notice.

cases.what: The provider's ingest session creation carries the distribution session in mbsDisSessInfos in the same POST and refuses a request whose mbsDisSessInfos is empty.

cases.what: The provider forwards a merge patch for an ingest session so that map entries can be added or removed (a null value removes the named entry); the form does not offer this, and a PUT from the form replaces the whole map with one entry.

cases.what: The form lets the SSM addresses (mbsSessionId) be edited and resends them in every PUT, with no check that they are unchanged.

cases.case: Other distribution session attributes updated only while INACTIVE
cases.what: The provider sends changed attributes in a PUT whatever the state of the distribution session; its only guard is a confirmation click when the state itself changes.

requirements.name: MBSTF / MBSTF subfunctions to support Packet Distribution Method

cases.case: Reformatting of ingested packets for MBS transmission
cases.what: In Proxy mode the MBSTF rewrites the UDP/IP headers of ingested payloads to the MBS source, group address and port; in Forward-only mode it forwards whole IP packets, re-fragmented to the tunnel MTU.

requirements.name: MBS User Services distribution methods / Packet Distribution Method

cases.case: Packet sequence numbering and/or FEC redundancy added by the MBSTF
cases.what: The MBSTF adds neither sequence numbers nor FEC to packet distribution; the FEC hooks are empty stubs.

cases.case: Forward-only mode: transport protocol on top of IP opaque to the MBS system
cases.what: Forward-only mode forwards ingested IPv4/IPv6 packets unchanged, but the ingest path parses each packet as UDP: the Packet(msghdr) constructor, used because PacketForwardOnlyController expects encapsulated packets, walks IPv6 next-header fields until it meets IPPROTO_UDP (with a different, unscaled length step than the other constructor), so an IPv6 packet carrying TCP or another protocol is not treated as opaque and the walk reads past its headers.

cases.case: The Packet Distribution Session may be operated in one of two different modes:
cases.what: The MBSTF has one controller for PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY (IP packets forwarded as new IP packets) and one for PACKET_PROXY (UDP payloads forwarded in new UDP packets), each rejecting a session of the other mode.

requirements.name: Re-using MBMS Delivery Method as Packet Distribution Method / General

cases.case: Proxy mode: UDP payloads handled and forwarded, possibly on different UDP ports
cases.what: In Proxy mode the MBSTF takes UDP payloads from ingest and forwards them into the distribution session with its own source, destination and port taken from the session SSM parameters.

cases.case: Forward-only mode: complete IP packets forwarded as MBS PDUs
cases.what: In Forward-only mode the MBSTF receives complete IP packets and forwards them unchanged as MBS PDUs towards the MB-UPF tunnel.

cases.case: For the Packet Distribution Method, the MBSTF may handle the ingested content on two ...
cases.what: Proxy mode handles UDP payloads with a UDP-level packetiser and forward-only mode handles whole IP packets, chosen from the provisioned pktDistributionOperatingMode.

cases.case: Proxy mode: client makes UDP payloads available to the MBS-Aware Application
cases.what: No UDP payloads are received or exposed to the application; packet distribution is a logging stub.

cases.case: Single-shot object delivery

cases.what: CAROUSEL mode repeats the manifest objects in FLUTE at their repetition intervals and replaces an object when a new version is ingested or the manifest changes.

cases.case: Pull acquisition: session parameters cite object URLs
cases.what: Pull URLs are turned into fetch URLs only when objIngestBaseUrl is present (the path is appended to it); with no base URL the fetch URL stays empty, so an absolute URL in objAcquisitionIdsPull is never fetched.

cases.what: The MBSTF accepts a single manifest URL per session, carries no content type with the identifier (the Rel-18 objAcquisitionIdsPull is a plain URI list) and determines the type from the fetched Content-Type; it has no notion of several entry points of different types.

cases.case: Entry point document and ancillary objects ingested and transmitted
cases.what: In streaming mode the MPD, initialisation segments and media segments are ingested and sent in the FLUTE session, but each item is popped from the list packager once and sent once; the MPD is re-sent only when it is re-fetched (a dynamic MPD with minimumUpdatePeriod) and initialisation segments are pulled once, so there is no repetition pattern.

cases.case: Appropriate repetition pattern for the entry point document and ancillary objects
cases.what: STREAMING mode sends each object once (and again only when the manifest changes); there is no repetition pattern for the entry point or ancillary objects.

requirements.name: General / Object manifest

cases.case: Per-object attributes of the object manifest maintained by the MBSTF
cases.what: The MBSTF keeps the parsed manifest objects (locator, repetition interval, keep-updated interval, earliest and latest fetch times) and uses each in scheduling fetches and repetition.

cases.case: updateInterval of the object manifest, ignored for push
cases.what: The manifest updateInterval schedules a manifest refetch only when pull acquisition is provisioned; for push acquisition it is not used.

cases.case: objects: list of objects to be carouselled
cases.what: Objects listed in the manifest are fetched and added to the carousel packager, but when a replacement manifest drops an object it is erased from the object store only; the packager keeps its PackageItem (a shared pointer) and keeps carouselling it, because updateCarousel (the only code that removes packager items) runs only when the packager is created.

cases.case: locator: URL from which the object is ingested
cases.what: Each manifest object is fetched from its locator URL.

cases.case: repetitionInterval of an object
cases.what: The carousel repeats each object at its repetitionInterval (converted from milliseconds); where omitted the MBSTF allocates the remaining bit rate; there is no collection mode that would ignore it.

cases.case: keepUpdatedInterval: cache control takes precedence
cases.what: After each fetch the next check time is the earlier of the origin cache expiry and the object time plus keepUpdatedInterval, so the interval overrides a longer cache lifetime instead of yielding to it.

cases.case: keepUpdatedInterval omitted: no update checks
cases.what: When keepUpdatedInterval is omitted the MBSTF still schedules refetches at the cache expiry of the object (default 10 s or 10 min when the origin gives none), rather than not checking.

cases.case: Detected changes reflected and signalled
cases.what: A refetch is a conditional request using the stored ETag and Last-Modified; a changed object replaces the stored one and is re-sent in FLUTE with new metadata.

cases.case: earliestFetchTime: not fetched before this time
cases.what: The next fetch time of an object is held back to its earliestFetchTime.

cases.case: latestFetchTime: fetched no later than this time
cases.what: Objects are scheduled for fetch from now (or earliestFetchTime) and an object whose latestFetchTime has passed is not fetched.

cases.case: Availability start time = ingest time plus configured distribution offset
cases.what: The MBSTF keeps no availability start time or distribution offset for objects.

cases.case: Availability end time = ingest time plus configured clean-up time
cases.what: The object end time is the origin cache expiry (or a fixed default of 10 s for pull and 10 min for push), not a configured clean-up time added to the ingest time.

cases.what: STREAMING mode accepts an object manifest (media type application/3gpp-mbs-object-manifest+json) and ingests the objects it lists.

cases.what: STREAMING mode accepts a DASH MPD (media type application/dash+xml), derives the media and initialisation segments to fetch from it and refreshes it.

cases.what: The MPD, its initialisation segments and its media segments are all ingested by the same controller and sent in the same FLUTE session.

cases.what: In STREAMING mode each object, including the MPD and initialisation segments, is sent once and the MPD again only when it is updated; there is no periodic retransmission for late joiners.

cases.what: An updated MPD is detected (pull refetch at the update period, or a new push), applied to the segment list and sent in the FLUTE session as soon as it is ingested.

cases.what: The MBSTF fetches each DASH segment at its origin availability start time and then sends it, so its last packet reaches the client after that time; no distribution offset or deadline scheduling against the client-side availability start time exists.

cases.what: libflute sends a new FDT Instance whenever a file is added or removed and repeats it on a timer, listing the files currently queued.

cases.what: The Content-Location of each file is the object fetched URL (rewritten with the distribution base URL when configured), which is the URL the segment was requested from, including for DASH segment URLs resolved from the MPD.

cases.case: URL rewritten using the Object distribution base URL
cases.what: When both base URLs are set and the object URL starts with the ingest base URL, the ingest base is replaced by the distribution base in the FDT Content-Location.

cases.what: An updated manifest or MPD object is sent as a FLUTE file whose Content-Location is derived from its fetched URL in the same way as other objects, so it matches the entry point URL.

cases.case: File Expires no later than the latest availability start time
cases.what: libflute writes no per-File Expires attribute; the FDT Instance Expires is twice the FDT repeat interval from now, and the per-file value is the cache-control Expires element.

cases.case: Cache-Control Expires used for the availability end time
cases.what: The Cache-Control Expires of each transmitted object is the object's HTTP cache expiry (origin max-age less age, a configured default, or the pushed Expires), not the object's availability end time.

cases.case: Content-MD5 and File-ETag optionally used
cases.what: libflute always computes and writes Content-MD5 for each file, and the packager passes the object ETag so that mbms2012:File-ETag is written when the object has one.

cases.case: For each object associated with the object flow to be delivered in the MBS ...
