features.name: Distribution Session control in the MBSTF

requirements.name: Domain model / Static information model

cases.case: MB-UPF ingest information from the MB-SMF response given to the MBSTF
cases.what: The tunnel address returned by the MB-SMF is placed in the MBSTF distribution session as the MB-UPF tunnel address together with the traffic flow information.

cases.case: TMGI allocated only if not already allocated
cases.what: A TMGI is always requested from the MB-SMF; an AF-supplied TMGI is not used to skip allocation.

requirements.name: Domain model / MBS Distribution Session parameters

cases.case: Distribution Session Identifier unique within the MBS User Service
cases.what: The MBSF generates a random UUID as the distribution session identifier, so it is unique across all MBS User Services.

cases.case: State: INACTIVE, ESTABLISHED, ACTIVE
cases.what: The state of each distribution session is computed from the schedule as INACTIVE, ESTABLISHED or ACTIVE, stored in the session information and reported to the AF and the MBSTF.

cases.case: State: DEACTIVATING
cases.what: The MBSF never sets DEACTIVATING as the state of a distribution session; it rejects it when supplied and only tracks it as a last reported MBSTF state.

cases.case: One MBS Session Context per distribution session
cases.what: Each distribution session has exactly one MBSMFMBSSession (MBS Session Context) at the MB-SMF.

cases.case: Several MBS Session Contexts when multiple target service areas are specified
cases.what: Multiple target service areas of one distribution session are sent in a single MBS Session; no separate contexts are created per area.

cases.case: MB-UPF tunnel endpoint address
cases.what: The MBSF asks the MB-SMF for a tunnel and passes the returned MB-UPF address and port to the MBSTF.

cases.case: MBMS GW tunnel endpoint address (SGi-mb)
cases.what: The MBSF has no MBMS GW / EPC interworking and never handles an MBMS GW tunnel address.

cases.case: User Plane traffic flow information (source, multicast destination, port)
cases.what: The MBSTF receives the SSM source and destination address and a random UDP port as traffic flow information, and none for packet Forward-only mode.

cases.case: MBS Session Identifier: TMGI allocated with the MB-SMF
cases.what: A TMGI is allocated through the MB-SMF and put in the session's MbsSessionId next to the SSM address.

cases.case: MBS Session Identifier: TMGI supplied by the MBS Application Provider
cases.what: An AF-supplied TMGI is not honoured: a distribution session without an SSM address is not provisioned, and one with an SSM address still gets a TMGI requested.

cases.case: Same MBS Session Identifier shared by location-dependent distribution sessions
cases.what: Distribution sessions may share one MBS Session Identifier when their service areas do not overlap; overlapping use is refused.

cases.case: Multiplexed distribution sessions share one MBS Session
cases.what: multiplexedServFlag is stored and echoed but no multiplexing is done; every distribution session gets its own MBS Session, and identical session identifier and areas are refused.

cases.case: Same MBS Session Identifier for all sessions in the multiplex
cases.what: No multiplex is formed, so no common MBS Session Identifier is assigned to a set of distribution sessions.

cases.case: AL-FEC scheme identified by an RMT URI term
cases.what: The MBSF passes the AF's fecScheme to the MBSTF unchecked; it builds no AL-FEC scheme identifier of its own and does not validate that the value is an RMT FEC encoding URI.

cases.case: Additional scheme-specific AL-FEC parameters
cases.what: The MBSF forwards the whole FEC configuration, including the additional name-value parameters, from the AF's request to the MBSTF.

cases.case: Transport security protection flag
cases.what: The MBSF has no transport security protection flag: it neither reads one from the AF nor passes one to the MBSTF.

cases.case: MB-UPF or MBMS GW tunnel address present
cases.what: The MBSF requests a tunnel from the MB-SMF and always sends the MB-UPF tunnel address in the MBSTF create request; it never sends an MBMS GW address.

cases.case: Announcement associated with a session in ESTABLISHED or ACTIVE state
cases.what: The announcement is built only when all distribution sessions of the ingest session are ESTABLISHED or ACTIVE, not per distribution session.

cases.case: User Plane traffic flow information with transport session identifier (object distribution)
cases.what: For object distribution the traffic flow information sent to the MBSTF carries a transport session identifier assigned by the MBSF.

cases.case: Object acquisition method: push or pull
cases.what: The PULL or PUSH acquisition method is passed to the MBSTF and decides how the acquisition identifiers are sent.

cases.case: Object acquisition identifiers forwarded
cases.what: The acquisition identifiers from the AF are forwarded to the MBSTF as pull URL paths or as the push identifier.

cases.case: Content type accompanying each object acquisition identifier
cases.what: No content type accompanies the identifiers; contentTypes does not exist in the Rel-18 model.

cases.case: Object ingest base URL for push nominated by the MBSF and unique
cases.what: For push the ingest base URL is assigned by the MBSTF and the MBSF does not nominate it; the code that would copy it into the AF response never runs.

cases.case: Object ingest base URL for pull nominated by the MBS Application Provider
cases.what: The AF-supplied objIngUri for pull sessions is forwarded to the MBSTF as the base for relative acquisition identifiers.

cases.case: Packet ingest method passed to the MBSTF and returned listen address merged
cases.what: The ingest method is sent to the MBSTF and the listen address and tunnel address the MBSTF returns for unicast ingest are merged into the endpoint addresses in the response.

cases.case: Multicast ingest valid for Proxy mode only
cases.what: The combination of multicast ingest with Forward-only mode is not checked or rejected.

cases.case: MBSTF ingest endpoint addresses supplied by the AF and passed on
cases.what: The AF-supplied ingest endpoint addresses are passed to the MBSTF and completed with the MBSTF addresses in the response.

cases.case: SSM endpoint nominated by the MBSF when the AF gives none
cases.what: The MBSF never nominates ingest endpoint addresses; ingEndpointAddrs is a required AF attribute.

cases.case: MBS FSA Identifier in the distribution session
cases.what: mbsFSAId is set on the MB-SMF MBS Session.

cases.case: Target UE classes of the distribution session
cases.what: nrRedCapUeInfo is accepted and echoed but never passed to the MB-SMF.

cases.case: QoS information (5QI) applied to the traffic flow
cases.what: The MBSF passes the QoS information (including the 5QI) to the MB-SMF inside the MBS Session it creates; it does not interact with a PCF at Nmb12 to set the QoS.

cases.case: MBSF sets the QoS with the PCF at Nmb12
cases.what: The MBSF has no Nmb12 interaction with a PCF.

cases.case: Maximum content bit rate
cases.what: maxContBitRate is sent to the MBSTF as the session bit rate.

cases.case: Maximum content delay
cases.what: maxContDelay is sent to the MBSTF as the session maximum delay.

cases.case: Distribution method
cases.what: The distribution method selects object or packet distribution data for the MBSTF.

cases.case: Operating mode
cases.what: The object or packet operating mode is sent to the MBSTF.

cases.case: Traffic marking information
cases.what: trafficMarkingInfo is sent to the MBSTF as the DSCP marking for packets sent to the MB-UPF.

cases.case: Service areas disjoint from other sessions sharing the MBS Session Identifier
cases.what: A new distribution session whose MBS Session Identifier and service area overlap another is refused at creation and when added by an update, but an update that changes the target service areas of an existing distribution session is applied with no overlap check and without updating the registry, and two overlapping sessions inside one create request pass validation.

cases.case: One MBS Session Context per declared service area
cases.what: All service areas of a distribution session go into a single MBS Session; no per-area context or Area Session Identifier is handled.

cases.case: NOTE: When the MBS Application Provider is outside the trust domain these may be ...
cases.what: The MBSF accepts extTgtServAreas with geographic areas and civic addresses and passes them to the MB-SMF session.

requirements.name: Domain model / MBS User Service Announcement parameters

cases.case: Distribution session announcements in the user service announcement
cases.what: The announcement contains one distribution session description for every distribution session of the ingest session.

requirements.name: Domain model / MBS Distribution Session Announcement parameters

cases.case: Announcement MBS Session Identifier (TMGI or SSM)
cases.what: The SDP file referenced by each distribution session description carries the TMGI and the SSM source and destination of the session.

cases.case: FSA Identifier in the announcement
cases.what: mbsFSAId is put in the availability information of the distribution session description.

cases.case: Radio parameters obtained from the OAM
cases.what: The MBSF has no OAM interface and puts no radio parameters in announcements.

cases.case: Distribution method in the announcement
cases.what: Each distribution session description carries the distribution method of the session.

cases.case: Session Description parameters in the announcement
cases.what: Each distribution session description has a session description locator pointing to an SDP file with the FLUTE media, bandwidth, TSI and source filter needed for reception.

cases.case: Service protection description
cases.what: No service protection or key management parameters are put in announcements.

cases.case: Target UE classes in the announcement
cases.what: The availability information never carries NR RedCap UE information.

requirements.name: Domain model / Mapping of MBS Distribution Session to MBS Session Context

cases.case: Table 4.5.9-1: state to MBS activity status
cases.what: ACTIVE and ESTABLISHED are mapped to an active MB-SMF activity status and other states to inactive.

cases.case: Table 4.5.9-1: SSM address and TMGI
cases.what: The SSM source and destination address from the session identifier are set on the MBS Session and a TMGI is requested.

cases.case: Table 4.5.9-1: MBS service area, FSA ID and location-dependent flag
cases.what: The target service areas, external service area, FSA identifier and locationDependent flag are copied to the MB-SMF MBS Session.

cases.case: Table 4.5.9-1: NR RedCap UE information
cases.what: NR RedCap UE information is never copied to the MB-SMF MBS Session.

cases.case: Table 4.5.9-1: QoS flow information
cases.what: The service information containing the QoS is copied to the MB-SMF MBS Session.

cases.case: Table 4.5.9-2: MBS service type from the MBS User Service
cases.what: The MB-SMF MBS Session is always created with the multicast service type regardless of the service type of the MBS User Service.

cases.case: Table 4.5.9-2: activation and termination time from the active period
cases.what: The MBS activation and termination times are not set; activity is switched through the activity status instead.

cases.case: Table 4.5.9-2: service requirements or session information from the QoS information
cases.what: The MBS service information carrying the QoS is passed in the MBS Session create.

cases.case: Table 4.5.9-2: DNN and S-NSSAI selected by the MBSF
cases.what: The MBSF selects no DNN or S-NSSAI for the MBS Session.

requirements.name: Dynamic model / MBS Distribution Session life-cycle

cases.case: Distribution session INACTIVE when first provisioned
cases.what: The initial state follows the schedule or the requested state: ACTIVE with no schedule, ESTABLISHED or ACTIVE near or inside a window, INACTIVE only when the next window is far away.

cases.case: MBSF provisions a corresponding distribution session in the MBSTF
cases.what: The MBSF creates the corresponding distribution session at the MBSTF with a POST on the Nmbstf distribution session service.

cases.case: MBSTF replica also INACTIVE
cases.what: The MBSTF distribution session is created in the current computed state, which is not always INACTIVE.

cases.case: End date-time in the past: session expires and is no longer provisioned
cases.what: When every active window of the ingest session is in the past, the MBSF computes the INACTIVE state and keeps the distribution session provisioned; nothing expires it into a state in which it is no longer provisioned.

cases.case: End date-time before start date-time rejected at provisioning
cases.what: A time window whose stop time is before its start time is accepted without any check.

cases.case: Transition to ESTABLISHED shortly before the start
cases.what: From a configurable time before the window start the computed state is ESTABLISHED and a timer triggers the change to the MBSTF and MB-SMF.

cases.case: Establish the distribution session in the MBSTF over Nmb2
cases.what: After all MB-SMF sessions are created the MBSF posts the distribution session to the MBSTF with its ingest, traffic flow, tunnel and state data.

cases.case: On failure: error returned and reserved resources released
cases.what: A failure at the MB-SMF returns an error to the AF and deletes the created MBS Sessions; a failure at the MBSTF deletes the MBSTF session and then the MB-SMF session and returns an error.

cases.case: On failure: the distribution session returns to INACTIVE
cases.what: A failed creation destroys the ingest session and its distribution sessions instead of leaving them INACTIVE.

cases.case: Advertise via MBS-8 (PASSED_BACK)
cases.what: With PASSED_BACK the compiled announcement is returned to the AF once all sessions are ESTABLISHED or ACTIVE.

cases.case: Advertise via MBS-5 (VIA_MBS_5)
cases.what: The MBSF has no MBS-5 announcement service; the announcement is delivered only through the announcement carousel (MBS-4-MC) or passed back.

cases.case: Transition to ACTIVE at the start time
cases.what: At the window start, or immediately without a schedule, the computed state becomes ACTIVE and is applied to the MBSTF and the MB-SMF.

cases.case: Activation procedure on the MBSTF over Nmb2
cases.what: On the state change to ACTIVE the MBSF sends a PATCH of the distribution session state to the MBSTF.

cases.case: Severe error: transition to DEACTIVATING
cases.what: A service management or data ingest failure reported by the MBSTF returns the distribution session to INACTIVE; DEACTIVATING is never entered.

cases.case: Stop advertising the distribution session on deactivation
cases.what: Announcement bundles are kept when sessions go INACTIVE and are removed only when the ingest session is deleted.

cases.case: Deactivation procedure on the MBSTF over Nmb2
cases.what: At the end of an active window the MBSF patches the MBSTF distribution session state to INACTIVE; a DELETE goes directly to the MBSTF release.

cases.case: Release procedure on the MBSTF over Nmb2
cases.what: On deletion of an ingest session the MBSF sends a DELETE for each MBSTF distribution session.

cases.case: Expired session no longer provisioned after deactivation
cases.what: A session whose schedule has ended stays provisioned and INACTIVE; only an explicit DELETE removes it.

requirements.name: Procedures for User Service data transfer / MBS Distribution Session activation

cases.case: Activation of all distribution sessions at the next start time
cases.what: At the next window start, or at once without a schedule, every distribution session of the ingest session is activated at the MBSTF and the MB-SMF.

requirements.name: Procedures for User Service data transfer / MBS Distribution Session deactivation

cases.case: Deactivation of all distribution sessions at the next end time
cases.what: At the next window end every distribution session of the ingest session is set INACTIVE at the MBSTF and the MB-SMF.

requirements.name: Nmbstf_MBSDistributionSession service / Nmbstf_MBSDistributionSession_Update service operation

cases.case: Update: optional output MBS Distribution Session resource entity
cases.what: On a 200 reply to the Update the MBSF parses the body as a CreateRspData wrapper (object with a distSession member) instead of a bare DistSession, which is what the pinned Release 18 API returns for PATCH, so a conforming 200 body is rejected and the MBSF then deletes the session.

requirements.name: Nmbstf_MBSDistributionSession service / Nmbstf_MBSDistributionSession_StatusSubscribe operation

cases.case: MBSF monitors MBS Distribution Session events at the MBSTF
cases.what: The MBSF asks the MBSTF to report six event types by embedding a distSessionSubscription (event list, notify URI, correlation id) in the Create and Update bodies.

cases.case: Standalone StatusSubscribe operation (POST .../subscriptions)
cases.what: The MBSF never calls the StatusSubscribe operation on the subscriptions collection.

cases.case: Subscribe to multiple events in one subscription
cases.what: The subscription built by the MBSF lists six event types in one eventList.

requirements.name: Nmbstf_MBSDistributionSession service / Nmbstf_MBSDistributionSession_StatusSubscribeMod operation

cases.case: StatusSubscribeMod: modify an existing status subscription
cases.what: The MBSF never modifies a subscription at the MBSTF; it has no PATCH to a subscription resource.

requirements.name: Syntax and associated semantics / User Service Description data type

cases.case: distributionSessionDescriptions in the User Service Description
cases.what: The MBSF builds one Distribution Session Description per distribution session of the ingest session and adds them to the User Service Description it announces.

cases.case: Active period may be further restricted by SDP t lines
cases.what: The SDP the MBSF writes for each distribution session carries timing (t) lines taken from the active time range of the ingest session; no r lines are written.

requirements.name: Create / General

cases.case: Create: create a new MBS Distribution Session in the MBSTF
cases.what: The MBSF builds and sends a POST that creates the distribution session in a discovered MBSTF.

cases.case: Create uses HTTP POST
cases.what: The Create request is an HTTP POST to the dist-sessions collection of nmbstf-distsession v1.

cases.case: POST CreateReqData to the MBSTF dist-sessions collection
cases.what: The MBSF POSTs a CreateReqData to nmbstf-distsession/v1/dist-sessions whose DistSession holds the distribution session id and baseline parameters plus the object or packet distribution data.

cases.case: POST CreateReqData to the MBS Distribution Sessions collection
cases.what: The MBSF posts a CreateReqData with a distSession member to /dist-sessions.

cases.case: Baseline parameters including the Distribution Session Identifier
cases.what: The body carries distSessionId (a random UUID), state, tunnel address, maximum bit rate and optional delay, FEC and DSCP values.

cases.case: Object or packet distribution parameters
cases.what: Object distribution data is added for the OBJECT method and packet distribution data for the PACKET method.

cases.case: Create: create a new MBS Distribution Session in the MBSTF
cases.what: The MBSF builds and sends a POST that creates the distribution session in a discovered MBSTF.

requirements.name: Update / General

cases.case: Update: update an existing MBS Distribution Session
cases.what: The MBSF sends a PATCH that replaces the whole distSession or only its state when the session changes.

cases.case: Update uses HTTP PATCH
cases.what: The Update request is an HTTP PATCH with content type application/json-patch+json to /dist-sessions/{id}.

cases.case: PATCH request (PatchData) to update the session
cases.what: The MBSF sends a one-item JSON patch with op replace, either for the whole session or for its state.

cases.case: Update: update an existing MBS Distribution Session
cases.what: The MBSF sends a PATCH that updates the distribution session in the MBSTF.

requirements.name: Destroy / General

cases.case: Destroy: delete an existing MBS Distribution Session
cases.what: The MBSF sends a DELETE for each distribution session when the ingest session ends.

cases.case: Destroy uses HTTP DELETE
cases.what: The Destroy request is an HTTP DELETE to /dist-sessions/{id}.

cases.case: DELETE request (distSessionRef) to release the session
cases.what: The MBSF sends the DELETE with the session id it generated at Create as the last path segment.

cases.case: Destroy: delete an existing MBS Distribution Session
cases.what: The MBSF sends a DELETE that releases the distribution session in the MBSTF.

requirements.name: Retrieve / General

cases.case: Retrieve: retrieve parameters of an existing session
cases.what: The MBSF has no Retrieve call to the MBSTF.

cases.case: Retrieve uses HTTP GET
cases.what: The MBSF never sends a GET to a dist-sessions resource.

cases.case: GET request to the distribution session resource
cases.what: No GET request to the MBSTF is built anywhere in the MBSF.

cases.case: Retrieve: retrieve parameters of an existing session
cases.what: The MBSF has no Retrieve call to the MBSTF.

requirements.name: StatusSubscribe service operation / General

cases.case: StatusSubscribe operation used by the NF Service Consumer
cases.what: The MBSF does not call the StatusSubscribe operation.

cases.case: A subscription to MBSTF events is created
cases.what: A subscription is created through the distSessionSubscription member of the Create request.

cases.case: Create a subscription to MBSTF notifications for the session events
cases.what: The MBSF creates a subscription to six session events together with the distribution session.

requirements.name: StatusSubscribe service operation / Subscription creation

cases.case: Subscribe by HTTP POST to the subscriptions collection
cases.what: The MBSF sends no POST to a subscriptions collection; the subscription travels inside the Create body.

cases.case: POST StatusSubscribeReqData to the subscriptions collection
cases.what: StatusSubscribeReqData is never built or sent.

cases.case: Optional notification correlation ID in the subscription
cases.what: The embedded subscription carries a notifyCorrelationId made of the ingest session id and the distribution session key.

cases.case: Optional expiry time in the subscription
cases.what: The MBSF never sets an expiry time on the subscription.

cases.case: Subscription request content: list of events
cases.what: The embedded subscription lists the six event types.

cases.case: Subscription request content: Notification URI
cases.what: The embedded subscription carries a notifyUri that points at the MBSF notification listener.

cases.case: The payload body of the POST request shall contain:
cases.what: The MBSF never POSTs a StatusSubscribeReqData to the MBSTF subscriptions collection; it embeds a DistSessionSubscription (event list, notification URI, correlation id) in the distribution session create request instead.

requirements.name: StatusSubscribe service operation / Subscription update

cases.case: Update a subscription by HTTP PATCH
cases.what: The MBSF never updates a subscription at the MBSTF.

cases.case: PATCH to the individual subscription resource
cases.what: No request to /dist-sessions/{id}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId} is built.

requirements.name: StatusUnsubscribe / General

cases.case: StatusUnsubscribe operation used by the NF Service Consumer
cases.what: The MBSF never unsubscribes; it deletes the whole distribution session instead.

cases.case: Unsubscribe from MBSTF notifications for the session
cases.what: No unsubscribe request is sent; the subscription ends with the session Destroy.

cases.case: Unsubscribe by HTTP DELETE
cases.what: No DELETE is sent to a subscription resource.

cases.case: DELETE request to the individual subscription resource
cases.what: No request to the individual subscription resource is built.

requirements.name: StatusNotify / General

cases.case: StatusNotify: MBSTF notifies the subscribed consumer
cases.what: The MBSF listens for notifications from the MBSTF and processes the reported events.

cases.case: Events about an MBS distribution session are received
cases.what: The MBSF maps each reported event to a state change of the distribution session.

cases.case: Notification by HTTP POST to the callback URI given in the subscription
cases.what: The MBSF serves a POST callback at the URI it put in the subscription and finds the session from the two path segments.

cases.case: On success the MBSF returns 204 No Content
cases.what: After processing a notification the MBSF answers 204 with an empty body.

cases.case: JSON signalled by Content-Type application/json
cases.what: The Create request carries Content-Type application/json and a reply is accepted only if its content type is exactly application/json.

cases.case: JSON used for the HTTP bodies

requirements.name: Resources / Overview

cases.case: MBS Distribution sessions collection /dist-sessions (POST Create)
cases.what: The MBSF posts to the collection to create a session.

cases.case: Individual MBS Distribution session /dist-sessions/{distSessionRef} (PATCH Update)

requirements.name: Resource: MBS Distribution sessions collection (Collection) / Resource Definition

cases.case: Resource URI variables apiRoot and apiVersion
cases.what: apiVersion is fixed to v1 and the apiRoot comes from the discovered MBSTF instance.

requirements.name: Resource Standard Methods / POST

cases.case: POST URI query parameters (none defined)
cases.what: The Create request carries no query parameters, matching the table that lists none.

cases.case: POST request data structure CreateReqData
cases.what: The MBSF sends a CreateReqData body.

cases.case: POST response: 201 Created with CreateRspData
cases.what: The MBSF accepts 200 or 201 with a JSON body and reads it as CreateRspData.

cases.case: CreateReqData: representation of the session to be created
cases.what: The CreateReqData holds the DistSession the MBSF builds for the MBSTF.

cases.case: 201 Created: successful creation of an MBS session
cases.what: On 200 or 201 the MBSF stores the returned session and goes on with the ingest session.

requirements.name: Resource: Individual MBS distribution session (Document) / Resource Definition

cases.case: Resource URI variables apiRoot, apiVersion, distSessionRef
cases.what: apiVersion is v1 and the last segment is the session id the MBSF generated at Create.

requirements.name: Resource Standard Methods / PATCH

cases.case: PATCH URI query parameters (none defined)
cases.what: The PATCH carries no query parameters.

cases.case: PATCH response 204 No Content
cases.what: A 204 reply is treated as a failed update: the MBSF logs an error and rolls the state back.

cases.case: PATCH 204 No Content: successful response
cases.what: A 204 reply is handled as a failed update (error logged, rollback of the requested state).

requirements.name: Resource Standard Methods / DELETE

cases.case: DELETE URI query parameters (none defined)
cases.what: The DELETE carries no query parameters.

cases.case: DELETE request data structures (none)
cases.what: The DELETE has no body.

cases.case: DELETE response: 204 No Content
cases.what: On 204 the MBSF removes the transaction and marks the MBSTF session as deleted.

requirements.name: Resource Standard Methods / POST

cases.case: StatusSubscribeReqData: data within the StatusSubscribe request
cases.what: StatusSubscribeReqData is never built; the subscription is carried as a distSessionSubscription inside CreateReqData.

requirements.name: Resource Standard Methods / PATCH

cases.case: PATCH body for the status subscription
cases.what: The MBSF never updates a status subscription at the MBSTF: it creates the subscription inline and sends no PATCH to a subscription resource.

cases.case: Subscription PATCH carries a JSON Patch list for DistSessionSubscription
cases.what: The MBSF never sends a patch for a DistSessionSubscription.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: CreateReqData

cases.case: CreateReqData: MBS Distribution Session to be created
cases.what: CreateReqData carries the DistSession the MBSF builds.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: CreateRspData

cases.case: CreateRspData: representation of the created MBS session
cases.what: The MBSF reads the distSession member of the reply and stores it in the session context.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: DistSession

cases.case: distSessionId: assigned by the MBSF, unique in the MBS User Service
cases.what: The MBSF sets distSessionId to a fresh random UUID for each distribution session it creates.

cases.case: distSessionState: current state of the session
cases.what: The MBSF sets the state from the active-period logic or the requested state (INACTIVE, ESTABLISHED, ACTIVE or DEACTIVATING).

cases.case: mbUpfTunAddr: MB-UPF tunnel endpoint address
cases.what: The MBSF copies the tunnel IPv4 or IPv6 address and port obtained from the MB-SMF into mbUpfTunAddr.

cases.case: mbmsGwTunAddr: MBMS-GW tunnel endpoint address
cases.what: The MBSF never sets mbmsGwTunAddr.

cases.case: upTrafficFlowInfo: traffic flow details for the MBSTF
cases.what: The MBSF sets upTrafficFlowInfo for object distribution and for packet distribution in proxy mode, and leaves it out for PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY.

cases.case: mbr: maximum bit rate for the session
cases.what: The MBSF sends the maximum content bit rate it was given as mbr.

cases.case: maxDelay: maximum end-to-end distribution delay
cases.what: The MBSF sends the maximum content delay it was given as maxDelay.

cases.case: objDistributionData for the Object Distribution Method
cases.what: For the OBJECT method the MBSF sets objDistributionData.

cases.case: pktDistributionData for the Packet Distribution Method
cases.what: For the PACKET method the MBSF sets pktDistributionData when packet distribution info is present.

cases.case: dscpMarking: two-octet hexadecimal encoding with mask 0xFC
cases.what: The MBSF copies the Application Provider trafficMarkingInfo string unchanged into dscpMarking; it does not build the two-octet hexadecimal DSCP/mask (0xFC) form, and the sample value is a "direction=downlink;match=..." string.

cases.case: NOTE 1: objDistributionData or pktDistributionData present in a request
cases.what: Exactly one of the two is set according to the distribution method, and a session without the matching info is rejected when it is created.

cases.case: distSessionSubscription: request to subscribe to session events
cases.what: Create and Update bodies carry a distSessionSubscription with events, notify URI and correlation id.

cases.case: upTrafficFlowInfo: traffic flow details for the MBSTF
cases.what: The MBSF sets upTrafficFlowInfo for object distribution and for packet distribution in proxy mode, and leaves it out for PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdsPull: root objects to pull

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdPush: root object to push
cases.what: For the PUSH method the MBSF sets objAcquisitionIdPush to the first acquisition id of the ingest request when there is one.

cases.what: The MBSF copies objIngUri into objIngestBaseUrl and objDistrUri into objDistributionBaseUrl independently, so a request with a distribution base URL and no ingest URL is sent without objIngestBaseUrl; nothing enforces the conditional presence.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdPush present when provided for PUSH

cases.what: The MBSF copies objIngUri into objIngestBaseUrl and objDistrUri into objDistributionBaseUrl independently, so a request with a distribution base URL and no ingest URL is sent without objIngestBaseUrl; nothing enforces the conditional presence.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdPush present when provided for PUSH

cases.case: Push-based egest of objects to the MBS AS at MBS-12
cases.what: The MBSTF does not publish ingested objects to an MBS AS.

requirements.name: Dynamic model / MBS Distribution Session life-cycle

cases.case: MBSTF replica of the distribution session created INACTIVE
cases.what: A session created at the MBSTF passes through the INACTIVE state on creation (inputs set up, SESSION_DEACTIVATED event registered) and only moves on if the requested distSessionState is later than INACTIVE.

cases.case: A suitable error is returned to the MBSF when establishment fails
cases.what: Invalid configuration is refused synchronously with a 4xx error, but a failure to ingest from the upstream source after the session is created is reported only afterwards as a DATA_INGEST_FAILURE notification; the Create or Update itself has already succeeded.

cases.case: Resources released and the session returned to INACTIVE after failure
cases.what: After ingest failures the session returns to INACTIVE only after a number of consecutive failures (default 5, configurable); a packaging failure returns it to INACTIVE at once.

cases.case: Error conditions in ACTIVE state notified to the MBSF (Object Distribution Method)
cases.what: Object ingest failures and packaging failures are registered as DATA_INGEST_FAILURE and SERVICE_MANAGEMENT_FAILURE events and sent by StatusNotify to the subscribed MBSF.

cases.case: Error conditions in ACTIVE state notified to the MBSF (Packet Distribution Method)
cases.what: The packet controllers raise no ingest or packaging failure events, so packet-mode errors are not notified.

cases.case: Session moved to DEACTIVATING when the MBSF requests it
cases.what: When the MBSF sets distSessionState to DEACTIVATING (or INACTIVE) on an ACTIVE session the MBSTF stops output, drains the queue and then returns the session to INACTIVE.

requirements.name: Procedures for User Service data transfer / MBS Distribution Session activation

cases.case: Ingested content processed according to the distribution method
cases.what: The MBSTF packages ingested objects into FLUTE (list, carousel, streaming) or re-encapsulates ingested packets (proxy, forward-only).

cases.case: Optional computation of AL-FEC information
cases.what: No AL-FEC is computed.

cases.case: Severe ingest or distribution fault moves the session through DEACTIVATING to INACTIVE
cases.what: After repeated object ingest failures or on a packaging failure an ACTIVE session is set to INACTIVE, which passes through DEACTIVATING while the output is drained.

requirements.name: StatusSubscribe service operation / Subscription creation

cases.case: Notification URI: address to which the MBSTF sends notifications
cases.what: The notifyUri of the subscription (required by the model) is the address to which the MBSTF sends the notifications.

cases.case: Optional expiry time in the subscription request
cases.what: The subscription expiryTime is parsed into m_expiryTime and echoed in replies, but nothing reads it, so the subscription is never kept only for the requested time span nor expired.

cases.case: Optional Notification Correlation ID in the subscription request
cases.what: A notifyCorrelationId in the request is kept and sent back in the reportList of each notification.

cases.case: StatusSubscribe success: 201 Created
cases.what: A successful subscription returns 201 Created.

cases.case: Location header with the URI of the created subscription
cases.what: The 201 response carries a Location header made of the request URI plus the new subscription id.

cases.case: Failure response with ProblemDetails and cause for StatusSubscribe
cases.what: On failure the MBSTF returns an HTTP error with an application/problem+json ProblemDetails body whose cause is set from the error.

cases.case: ProblemDetails cause set for StatusSubscribe failures
cases.what: Failures (malformed request, unknown session) carry a ProblemDetails with a cause such as INVALID_MSG_FORMAT, MANDATORY_IE_MISSING or SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND.

cases.case: Request carries the list of events to subscribe to
cases.what: eventList is a required property of the subscription model, so a request without it is refused with 400.

cases.case: Request carries the Notification URI
cases.what: notifyUri is a required property of the subscription model, so a request without it is refused with 400.

cases.case: Response includes the distribution session identifier
cases.what: The subscription POST answers 201 with a Location header holding the request URI plus the new subscription id, so the distribution session identifier is conveyed; the StatusSubscribeRspData body has only subscription and reportList.

cases.case: Response includes the list of events successfully subscribed
cases.what: The returned subscription repeats the eventList of the stored subscription.

cases.case: Response includes the expiry time after which the subscription becomes invalid
cases.what: The response only echoes the expiryTime the consumer sent (if any); the MBSTF assigns no expiry of its own and never expires the subscription.

cases.case: The payload body of the POST response (StatusSubscribeRspData) shall include:
cases.what: The 201 response returns the request's subscription as received (events as requested, expiry only if the client supplied one) plus any immediate reports; it does not state the distribution session id, filter the events to those successfully subscribed, or set an expiry time.

cases.case: Collection of the individual subscriptions of a distribution session
cases.what: Each session holds a collection of subscriptions at /dist-sessions/{id}/subscriptions, created with POST.

cases.case: PATCH request body array(PatchItem)

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: CreateReqData

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: CreateRspData

cases.case: distSession in CreateRspData (mandatory)
cases.what: The 201 response body is a CreateRspData whose distSession is the stored session, built without the write-only attributes.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: DistSession

cases.case: distSessionId assigned by the MBSF
cases.what: The identifier supplied by the MBSF is mandatory, becomes the session key and the last element of the resource URI, and a second session with the same identifier is refused with 400.

cases.case: distSessionState (current state)
cases.what: The state in the session drives the state machine and is returned in the create, retrieve and update responses.

cases.case: mbUpfTunAddr used as the Nmb9 tunnel endpoint, packet distribution
cases.what: In packet distribution the tunnel address (IPv4 or IPv6) and port are read and used as the destination of the scheduler's output socket.

cases.case: mbUpfTunAddr used as the tunnel endpoint, object distribution, IPv4
cases.what: In object distribution the IPv4 tunnel address and port are passed to the object packager as the tunnel endpoint.

cases.case: mbUpfTunAddr as an IPv6 address, object distribution
cases.what: For object distribution only the ipv4Addr member of the tunnel address is read, so an IPv6 tunnel endpoint is ignored and no tunnel endpoint is passed to the packager.

cases.case: mbmsGwTunAddr
cases.what: The attribute is accepted by the model but nothing reads it, so no MBMS-GW tunnel endpoint is used.

cases.case: upTrafficFlowInfo required for object distribution and packet proxy mode
cases.what: A create request for object distribution or for PACKET_PROXY without upTrafficFlowInfo is refused with 400, and the values are used to build the output flow.

cases.case: mbr maximum bit rate
cases.what: Implemented; further detail is in the members-only section.

cases.case: maxDelay
cases.what: The attribute is accepted by the model but nothing reads it, so no delay bound is applied.

cases.case: objDistributionData for Object Distribution Method
cases.what: When objDistributionData is present the session is handled by an object controller (single, carousel or streaming) that reads its parameters.

cases.case: pktDistributionData for Packet Distribution Method
cases.what: When pktDistributionData is present the session is handled by a packet controller (proxy or forward-only) that reads its parameters.

cases.case: DSCP marking applied to outgoing traffic
cases.what: The attribute is accepted by the model but nothing reads it, so no DSCP or ToS marking is applied to outgoing traffic.

cases.case: dscpMarking encoding (two octets in hex, mask 0xFC)
cases.what: The value is carried as an unchecked string; its two-octet hexadecimal form and the 0xFC mask are not validated.

cases.case: Exactly one of objDistributionData and pktDistributionData
cases.what: A create request with neither or with both is refused with 400, and the response is built from the stored request so it carries the same one.

cases.case: distSessionSubscription in the create request
cases.what: A subscription carried in the create request is registered on the new session and used for notifications.

cases.case: upTrafficFlowInfo required for object distribution and packet proxy mode
cases.what: A create request for object distribution or for PACKET_PROXY without upTrafficFlowInfo is refused with 400, and the values are used to build the output flow.

cases.case: distSessionId assigned by the MBSF
cases.what: The identifier supplied by the MBSF is mandatory, becomes the session key and the last element of the resource URI, and a second session with the same identifier is refused with 400.

cases.case: distSessionState (current state)
cases.what: The state in the session drives the state machine and is returned in the create, retrieve and update responses.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: ObjDistributionData

cases.case: objDistributionOperatingMode SINGLE, CAROUSEL and STREAMING
cases.what: Each of these modes selects its own controller (list, carousel, streaming); the mode cannot be changed by a later update.

cases.case: objDistributionOperatingMode COLLECTION
cases.what: No controller handles the COLLECTION mode; a create request using it is answered with 501 Not Implemented.

cases.case: objAcquisitionMethod PULL
cases.what: With PULL the MBSTF creates pull ingesters that fetch the objects from the MBS Application Provider once the session is established.

cases.case: objAcquisitionMethod PUSH
cases.what: With PUSH the MBSTF starts a push ingester (HTTP receiver) that accepts the objects sent by the MBS Application Provider.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdsPull: paths relative to objIngestBaseUrl, pulled and distributed
cases.what: For a session in SINGLE operating mode the MBSTF joins each pull id to objIngestBaseUrl, fetches the object and distributes it; when objIngestBaseUrl is absent the resulting fetch URL is empty and the id is not fetched.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdPush: path relative to objIngestBaseUrl, pushed to the MBSTF
cases.what: A pushed object is accepted when its URL path equals objAcquisitionIdPush; other paths are refused with 400. The id is compared to the request path only, without the ingest base URL.

cases.case: objIngestBaseUrl replaced by objDistributionBaseUrl
cases.what: When both base URLs are present, the MBSTF replaces the ingest prefix of each object URL with the distribution base URL to derive the distribution location of the object.

cases.case: objDistributionBaseUrl replaces the ingest base URL
cases.what: The object location used for distribution is the distribution base URL followed by the part of the fetched URL that follows the ingest base URL.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdsPull relative to the ingest base URL
cases.what: Each pull path is joined to the ingest base URL and fetched; absolute URLs are skipped when a base URL is present, and carousel and streaming modes accept exactly one path.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdPush as root object path (carousel and streaming)
cases.what: The push path is joined to the ingest base URL to form the manifest URL and pushed objects must match it; when absent it defaults to 'manifest'.

cases.case: objIngestBaseUrl prefix replaced by the distribution base URL
cases.what: The ingest base URL is stored with each object and its prefix is swapped for the distribution base URL when the object is distributed.

cases.case: objIngestBaseUrl present when objDistributionBaseUrl is present (PUSH, set by the MBSTF)
cases.what: With PUSH the MBSTF fills in the ingest base URL of its push server and returns it in the create response.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdsPull present when provided for PULL (Release 19 wording)
cases.what: The MBSTF uses and returns objAcquisitionIdsPull for PULL sessions as it does for the Release 17 wording; the note-7 rule for SINGLE with PUSH is not part of this case.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdPush present when provided for PUSH (Release 19 wording)
cases.what: The MBSTF accepts objAcquisitionIdPush for PUSH sessions and only accepts a pushed object whose path matches it, as for the Release 17 wording; the note-7 rule for SINGLE with PUSH is not part of this case.

cases.case: objIngestBaseUrl prefix replaced by the distribution base URL
cases.what: The ingest base URL is stored with each object and its prefix is swapped for the distribution base URL when the object is distributed.

cases.case: objIngestBaseUrl present when objDistributionBaseUrl is present (PUSH, set by the MBSTF)
cases.what: With PUSH the MBSTF fills in the ingest base URL of its push server and returns it in the create response.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdsPull relative to the ingest base URL
cases.what: Each pull path is joined to the ingest base URL and fetched; absolute URLs are skipped when a base URL is present, and carousel and streaming modes accept exactly one path.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdPush as root object path (carousel and streaming)
cases.what: The push path is joined to the ingest base URL to form the manifest URL and pushed objects must match it; when absent it defaults to 'manifest'.

cases.case: objAcquisitionIdPush omitted with SINGLE mode and PUSH (NOTE 7)
cases.what: A create request with objAcquisitionIdPush in SINGLE mode with PUSH is rejected with 400.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: PktDistributionData

cases.case: pktDistributionOperatingMode PACKET_PROXY
cases.what: PACKET_PROXY selects a controller that ingests packets and re-addresses them with the configured source and destination before sending to the tunnel.

cases.case: pktDistributionOperatingMode PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY
cases.what: PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY selects a controller that forwards already-encapsulated ingested packets to the tunnel.

cases.case: pktIngestMethod selects unicast or multicast ingest
cases.what: UNICAST opens a unicast receiver tied to the AF address and MULTICAST joins the AF source-specific multicast group.

cases.case: mbStfIngestAddr for the Nmb8 ingest connection
cases.what: The AF egress tunnel address (unicast) or AF source-specific multicast address (multicast) is used to set up ingest, and the MBSTF's own listening address is written back into the same structure.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: StatusSubscribeReqData

cases.case: subscription in StatusSubscribeReqData
cases.what: The request body is parsed as StatusSubscribeReqData, its subscription is mandatory and is stored on the session.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: StatusSubscribeRspData

cases.case: subscription in StatusSubscribeRspData
cases.what: The 201 response carries the created subscription (without write-only attributes) in StatusSubscribeRspData.

cases.case: reportList with immediate event reports
cases.what: The 201 response includes a report list of already-occurred events of the subscribed types when there are any.

cases.case: reportList with immediate event reports
cases.what: The 201 response includes a report list of already-occurred events of the subscribed types when there are any.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: StatusNotifyReqData

cases.case: reportList in StatusNotifyReqData
cases.what: Each notification is a POST to the notify URI with a StatusNotifyReqData whose reportList holds the newly occurred subscribed events.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: DistSessionSubscription

cases.case: eventList stored and used to filter notifications
cases.what: The subscribed event types are mapped to flags and only events of those types are reported or notified.

cases.case: eventList in the response lists the events successfully subscribed
cases.what: The response echoes the requested list unchanged, including event types that the code does not recognise and ignores.

cases.case: notifyUri receives the notifications
cases.what: Notifications are posted to the notify URI given in the subscription, which is not echoed back (write-only).

cases.case: notifyCorrelationId
cases.what: The correlation identifier is stored (write-only) and is copied into every report list sent to the subscriber.

cases.case: Events stop generating notifications after expiryTime
cases.what: The expiry time is parsed and stored but never compared with the clock, so notifications continue after it.

cases.case: expiryTime in a subscription response
cases.what: The response repeats the requested expiry time unchanged, but the subscription never becomes invalid at that time.

cases.case: nfcInstanceId of the NF Service Consumer
cases.what: The identifier is accepted and stored with the subscription (write-only) and is not used further.

cases.case: distSessionSubscUri in the creation response
cases.what: When the creation request includes a subscription, the response carries distSessionSubscUri set to the URI of the new subscription resource.

cases.case: Location header of a separately created subscription
cases.what: The 201 response to a subscription POST carries a Location header made of the request URI and the new subscription identifier.

cases.case: distSessionSubscUri in the create response
cases.what: When the create request included a subscription, the 201 response carries the URI of the individual subscription resource in distSessionSubscUri.

cases.case: nfcInstanceId of the NF Service Consumer
cases.what: The identifier is accepted and stored with the subscription (write-only) and is not used further.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: DistSessionEventReportList

cases.case: eventReportList of DistSessionEventReport
cases.what: The report list is built with one report (type and timestamp) for each subscribed event that has occurred since the last report.

cases.case: notifyCorrelationId in DistSessionEventReportList
cases.what: The correlation identifier of the subscription, when it has one, is set on every report list that is sent or returned.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: DistSessionEventReport

cases.case: eventType in DistSessionEventReport
cases.what: Each report carries the type of the event that occurred (one of the six defined event types).

cases.case: timeStamp in DistSessionEventReport
cases.what: Each report carries the UTC time, in ISO 8601 form, at which the MBSTF recorded the event.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: UpTrafficFlowInfo

cases.case: destIpAddr multicast group destination address
cases.what: The destination address is used as the destination of the distributed traffic: it is written into the re-addressed UDP/IP headers in packet proxy mode and handed to the FLUTE transmitter in object mode.

cases.case: portNumber destination port
cases.what: The port is used as the UDP port of the distributed traffic in packet proxy mode and handed to the FLUTE transmitter in object mode.

cases.case: srcIpAddr required except in PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY
cases.what: A create request for object distribution or for a packet mode other than PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY without srcIpAddr is refused with 400, and the address is used as the source address of the distributed traffic.

cases.case: transportSessionId required for Object Distribution Method
cases.what: A create request for object distribution without transportSessionId is refused with 400, and the value is used as the transport session identifier of the object stream.

cases.case: transportSessionId is the 32-bit ALC TSI
cases.what: The value is truncated to 32 bits and passed as the transport session identifier of the FLUTE/ALC transmitter.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: MbStfIngestAddr

cases.case: afEgressTunAddr used to validate the source of incoming packets
cases.what: The AF egress address is used as the expected remote endpoint of the unicast ingest socket, and packets from any other source are dropped.

cases.case: afEgressTunAddr included for PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY and for PACKET_PROXY with UNICAST
cases.what: The missing address is detected, but the exception is thrown from the state transition outside the create handler's try blocks, so the request is not answered with a 400 error.

cases.case: mbStfIngressTunAddr returned for PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY
cases.what: For PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY the MBSTF writes the local address and port of its unicast ingest socket into mbStfIngressTunAddr, which is returned in the create and retrieve responses.

cases.case: afSsm joined for PACKET_PROXY with MULTICAST ingest
cases.what: The source-specific multicast address and port are used to open a receiver that joins the group (MCAST_JOIN_SOURCE_GROUP) for the given source.

cases.case: mbStfListenAddr returned for PACKET_PROXY with UNICAST
cases.what: For PACKET_PROXY with unicast ingest the MBSTF writes the local address and port of its ingest socket into mbStfListenAddr, which is returned in the create and retrieve responses.

cases.case: afEgressTunAddr used to validate the source of incoming packets
cases.what: The AF egress address is used as the expected remote endpoint of the unicast ingest socket, and packets from any other source are dropped.

cases.case: afEgressTunAddr present for PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY and for PACKET_PROXY with UNICAST
cases.what: The missing address is detected, but the exception is thrown from the state transition outside the create handler's try blocks, so the request is not answered with a 400 error.

cases.case: mbStfIngressTunAddr returned for PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY
cases.what: For PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY the MBSTF writes the local address and port of its unicast ingest socket into mbStfIngressTunAddr, which is returned in the create and retrieve responses.

cases.case: afSsm joined for PACKET_PROXY with MULTICAST ingest
cases.what: The source-specific multicast address and port are used to open a receiver that joins the group (MCAST_JOIN_SOURCE_GROUP) for the given source.

requirements.name: Structured data types / Type: ExtSsm

cases.case: ssm source and destination multicast addresses
cases.what: Both the multicast source address and the destination group address of the ssm are read and used for the multicast join.

cases.case: DistSessionState values INACTIVE, ESTABLISHED, ACTIVE, DEACTIVATING

cases.what: Each of these three values selects a controller that handles it.

cases.case: ObjDistributionOperatingMode COLLECTION
cases.what: No controller handles the COLLECTION value; a create request using it is answered with 501 Not Implemented.

requirements.name: Simple data types and enumerations / Enumeration: ObjAcquisitionMethod

cases.case: ObjAcquisitionMethod PULL
cases.what: PULL makes the MBSTF fetch the objects from the MBS Application Provider with pull ingesters.

cases.case: ObjAcquisitionMethod PUSH
cases.what: PUSH makes the MBSTF run a push ingester that receives the objects sent by the MBS Application Provider.

cases.case: ObjAcquisitionMethod values PULL and PUSH
cases.what: Both defined values are recognised and each starts its own ingest mechanism.

requirements.name: Simple data types and enumerations / Enumeration: PktDistributionOperatingMode

cases.case: PktDistributionOperatingMode PACKET_PROXY
cases.what: PACKET_PROXY selects the proxy controller.

cases.case: PktDistributionOperatingMode PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY
cases.what: PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY selects the forward-only controller.

requirements.name: Simple data types and enumerations / Enumeration: DistSessionEventType

cases.case: DistSessionEventType values
cases.what: All six event types are mapped to subscription flags and each is recorded by the session (activation, deactivation, ingest session established and terminated, ingest failure, service management failure).

requirements.name: Simple data types and enumerations / Enumeration: PktIngestMethod

cases.case: PktIngestMethod UNICAST
cases.what: UNICAST (also the default when absent) opens a unicast ingest receiver tied to the AF egress address.

cases.case: PktIngestMethod MULTICAST
cases.what: MULTICAST opens a receiver that joins the AF source-specific multicast group.

cases.what: The FDT writer has no code that emits a Group element.

cases.case: - Content-Encoding set to 'gzip'
cases.what: The MBSTF never requests gzip compression, so Content-Encoding gzip is never carried.

cases.case: - Content-Encoding attribute set to a value other than 'gzip'
cases.what: The MBSTF never sets a Content-Encoding, so no encoding other than gzip is announced.

requirements.name: MBMS Download Profile / FDT File-specific elements and attributes

cases.case: - mbms2007:Cache-Control
cases.what: mbms2007:Cache-Control is parsed into the file entry but never used by the client (no expiry or no-cache handling).

cases.case: - Content-MD5
cases.what: Content-MD5 is read per file and the received data is checked against it; a mismatch discards the symbols and reception restarts.

cases.case: - Content-Location
cases.what: Content-Location is required on every File and is normalised to a path that keys the stored object and the local content URL.

cases.case: - TOI
cases.what: TOI is required on every File and selects the reception object for incoming packets.

cases.case: - Content-Length
cases.what: Content-Length is read and, when Transfer-Length is absent, used to size the transfer.
